The classic Crossy Road arcade game, made for your Garmin device. Hop your character across endless roads, rivers, and railways without getting hit. Collect coins and use them to purchase up to 20 different characters! (Some low-memory devices will have 10 characters instead).

--- How to play ---

Move forward to score points with the controls listed below. Dodge traffic, time your jumps across logs and lily pads, and avoid getting hit by trains. Don't stand still too long or the eagle will snatch you. Collect coins scattered on the ground to use to purchase new characters. How far can you go?

--- Button controls (configurable in settings) ---

- START: move up

- BACK: move down

- UP: move right

- DOWN: move left

- Hold BACK: exit to main menu

Open settings to change what each button does!

--- Touch controls (configurable in settings) ---

Tap mode:

- Tap the top, left, right, or bottom of the screen to move in that direction.

- Swipe right to exit to the main menu.

Swipe mode:

- Swipe up, down, left, or right to move in that direction.

- Hold to exit to main menu

--- Customize ---

From the home screen, press the settings icon or UP, then select "Customize."

In the customize menu, you can pay 100 coins to purchase a random character that you have not unlocked yet. To select a character, scroll through the menu by tapping the left and right arrow icons or by using UP and DOWN, then tap on the character you wish to select or press START.

Exit the customize menu by pressing BACK or swiping right.

--- Settings ---

From the home screen, press the settings icon or UP, then select "Settings."

- Sound: on / off

- Vibration: on / off

- Touch controls: tap or swipe mode

- Button controls: opens a sub-menu to let you change what each button does

- Graphics quality: 2D / 3D

Exit settings with the BACK button or by swiping right.

naam: Neon Rush: Gravity Flip Runner Game
besch:
A one-button neon arcade runner for your Garmin watch. Run along the floor or the ceiling of a glowing corridor and flip gravity to dodge the spikes. Flip the rush: how far can you go?

HOW TO PLAY
• Buttons: START, UP or DOWN flip gravity. BACK pauses.
• Touch: tap anywhere to flip. Gravity flips the moment your finger touches the screen.
• Flip any time, even mid-air. Spikes cost a life on contact, so get to the other side in time.
• Ride on top of blocks, but don't run into their fronts. Land on platforms to cross spikes on both walls.

FEATURES
• Fair by design: every obstacle leaves you time to flip, while the speed rises as you go.
• Six colour worlds, a new one about every half minute: Neon Pulse, Toxic Run, Cyber Blue, Lava Rush, Sunset Drive and Ultraviolet.
• Neon glow, parallax stars and a flash for every close dodge.
• Collect gems and unlock ten skins, from the Orb to the Comet.
• Power-ups: a heart for an extra life (up to three), a magnet that pulls in gems, and ×2 gems.
• Neon graphics tuned for each watch, from AMOLED to MIP screens.
• Vibration, sound and effects, set on the watch or in the Garmin Connect app.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Offline game. No Pacelyo account, tracking or subscription. Your progress stays on the watch.
• Interface in 36 languages, following your watch language.
• Neon Rush is a game: play it while resting, not while running or cycling.

Support: info@pacelyo.com

A boulder blocks the middle lane. Gold glints on the right. How late will you switch?

Ruin Run is a three-lane endless runner for your Garmin watch. Dash across a mossy jungle bridge, dodge rolling boulders, and collect coins as the pace picks up. Reach 800 m to enter the glowing Ember Ruins.

Grab magnets to pull in coins from every lane, use a shield to survive a hit, or sprint straight through the rocks. Complete goals for bonus coins and spend them on new runner outfits, upgrades, head starts, and revives.

Swipe left or right, tap either side of the touchscreen, or use UP and DOWN on button models to change lanes. Your best distance is saved on your watch. Can you beat it on the next run?

The watch hides a colour code; you crack it. Guess, read the clues, guess again. And when you are tired of guessing, hide a code yourself and watch the watch crack yours.

Värikäs is Finnish for colourful.

Colours mode
4 pegs, 6 colours, colours may repeat, 10 guesses. After every guess: a filled dot for each peg in the right place, a ring for each right colour in the wrong place.

Order mode
5 balls, each colour exactly once. You only have to find the order. Swap balls into place; the only clue is how many are already right.

The watch guesses
Set a secret code and watch the watch crack it, usually in four or five guesses.

Custom
Choose 3 to 6 pegs, 6 to 8 colours, 8 to 12 guesses, and whether colours may repeat. Records are kept for each setup.

Also
- Painted neon pegs, and a unique symbol for every colour, so it works for colour-blind players too.
- Buttons or touch.
- English, Hebrew, German, French, Spanish.

naam: Kaiku: Echo the Lights, a Neon Memory Game
besch:
The watch plays a sequence of lights; you echo it back. Every round it grows by one. And because every pad has its own vibration, you can close your eyes and play by feel alone. A memory game for the wrist that no screen can give you on its own.

Kaiku is Finnish for echo.

Four painted neon pads
Polished metallic pads in jade, fire orange, sea blue and gold. Each pad also has its own symbol, so the game works for colour-blind players too.

naam: Mu Torere: Māori Star Board Game in Neon
besch:
A board game with eight points and one empty spot, played by the Māori of Aotearoa New Zealand long before anyone drew it in neon. The rules fit in four sentences. Beating the watch on Master is impossible, and that is the fun of it.

How it plays
You and the watch each have four pieces on the points of the star. On your turn you move one piece into the only empty spot: a neighbouring point, or the centre (putahi). A piece may enter the centre only when it stands next to a rival piece. Whoever cannot move loses. The same position three times is a draw.

The watch
Three levels. Easy and Medium make mistakes. Master plays a perfect, fully solved game and cannot be beaten; a draw is the best you can do, and holding one is a small victory. Your record (won, lost, drawn) is kept for each level.

Also
- Buttons or touch.
- Gold rings show which pieces can move.
- Who starts alternates every game.
- Quick games, a few minutes each.
- English, Hebrew, German, French, Spanish.

Basically we have a wolf named Volk, and four hens. Hens continuously lay eggs and we help Volk to catch the eggs by directing its basket to hens. The score is the number of collected eggs. An idle game asks the same question over and over: what to buy next. Then it hides the answer behind numbers nobody can compare in their head. A machine at 4.1e17 coins that adds 9.2e14 a second, against an upgrade at 8.8e16 that doubles something older. Most people give up and buy whatever is newest, which is usually the wrong answer.

Coglet works that comparison out. Every purchase on offer, a machine, a hundred of them at once, an upgrade, a manager, a wider away window, is scored the same way: production added per day against coins spent, which comes out as a payback time. That one figure is what lets a machine, an upgrade and a manager be ranked against each other at all. The front page names the shortest payback standing, what it costs and how long it takes to earn itself back, or how long until the balance covers it. The rebuild screen answers the other question the genre never answers: whether prestige is worth taking now, and how long it takes to get back to where the factory already is.

WHAT IT DOES
- Twelve machines on their own cost curves, each kind doubling its output every 25 built
- An advisor that ranks every purchase by payback time and names the best one
- Twelve upgrade levels per machine, a manager per machine, and a night shift that widens the away window from eight hours to sixteen and then to twenty-four
- Buy max priced from the closed form of the geometric series, so a few hundred units cost one multiplication rather than a loop the watchdog would cut short
- Offline earnings settled from the wall clock in one multiplication, capped at the away window, with machines that have no manager idling at a quarter speed
- A clock set backwards pays exactly nothing, so absence cannot be farmed
- A rebuild that trades the whole run for a permanent multiplier, with a screen that says plainly whether it is worth it now and when it pays back
- Every coin carried as a mantissa and an exponent, and printed with a short suffix, K, M, B, T and on through letter pairs, never as scientific notation
- Four pages: the floor, what each machine is producing, what to buy next, the rebuild
- Five languages, on-watch settings, nothing sent anywhere

Nothing but the watch. No phone, no signal, no account.

naam: Dicewise - Yatzy and Farkle dice games

Dicewise puts three dice games on your watch: Scandinavian Yatzy, American-style Yatzy US and Farkle, alone or with up to four players passing the watch around, against computer players on three levels. Every throw comes from one seeded generator that serves all players in turn order, the seed is on screen, and the same seed replays the same dice, so you can check that nobody gets better luck. The computer players see exactly what you see and only differ in how well they choose.

Behind each roll sits an expected-value engine. In both Yatzy variants it works out, over the rolls you have left, which dice are worth holding; in Farkle it weighs banking against rolling on with the dice that remain. Ask for a hint and it marks the dice and names the box. After the game the analysis shows how many points each of your choices cost compared to the best one, and which moves were the most expensive.

- Yatzy (15 boxes, 50 bonus at 63), Yatzy US (13 boxes, 35 bonus, Yatzy bonus and Joker rules) and Farkle (to 10,000 or 5,000, hot dice, final round)
- 1 to 4 players on one watch, each seat a player or a computer opponent (easy, normal, hard)

The most-reviewed word game on this platform is a Wordle clone, and the reviews all say the same thing: the letters are too small to hit. A twenty-six key keyboard on a 45 mm watch leaves each key about three millimetres of glass, which is half a fingertip. That is not difficulty. That is a typo, then another one, and then the app is uninstalled.

Lexil has no keyboard. There are seven letters and nothing else: six on a ring and one in the middle, each tile about a fifth of the screen across and roughly ten times the target area of a key. Words run from four letters up, any letter may be used again, and every word has to use the one in the middle, which is what stops seven big buttons from being a small game. Using all seven in a single word is a pangram and pays seven extra.

WHAT IT DOES

- Four hundred puzzles held on the watch, one a day, averaging thirty-one words each
- Five ranks, Beginner through to Genius, each cut at a share of that day's own point total, so Great means the same amount of work on a twenty-word day as on a forty
- Four letters score one point, longer words score their length, a pangram adds seven, so a rank cannot be reached by grinding out the easy words
- Shuffle the six outer letters: the same set in a new order reads as a new puzzle

Most picture cross puzzles are generated rather than written, and a generated one usually has a hole in it: a place where two arrangements both fit the numbers and the only way on is to pick one. Half an hour of careful counting, and then a coin toss.

Pixara does not show a picture until a line solver has finished it from a blank grid.
That solver does only what a person does with a strip of cells and a list of block lengths: work out every arrangement the numbers still allow, keep the cells that are filled in all of them, cross out the cells that are empty in all of them, and go round the rows and columns until nothing changes. If it stalls, that picture is thrown away and another is painted. A solver that finishes also proves the answer unique, so the picture the numbers describe is the only picture there is.

WHAT IT DOES
- Every picture proved solvable by pure logic before it is ever drawn
- Three sizes: five by five, eight by eight, and a ten by ten that takes real time
- The clue for the aimed row and the aimed column is always spelled out in full and enlarged, because a paper clue strip does not fit round glass
- Aim, then tap: the first tap frames a cell, wider than the cell so it stays visible around a fingertip; the second fills it, holding it crosses it out
- Works the same with buttons on watches with no touch screen
- Filling a cell that is not in the picture costs thirty seconds on the clock
- A hint that names the row or the column proving the next cell, and then marks it
- A daily picture taken from the calendar date, the same one on every watch, rotating through the three sizes
- The grid is written down after every move, so leaving the app never loses it
- Best time per size, pictures finished against pictures started, and a run of dailies
- Five languages, on-watch settings, nothing sent anywhere

WHAT IT NEEDS
Nothing but the watch. No phone, no signal, no account.

The object of the game is to discard everything but the aces! Wild cards will appear below the deck as you earn them, after every 12 discards, up to the limit you set before starting the game.  To use one, tap it to highlight it.  The available cards to discard will also be highlighted.  Either tap one of them, or tap the wild again to cancel using it.

It's Mastermind!  Play anywhere, on the go!  And best of all, it's completely free!

Mastermind is a logic game where you try to guess the color and order of pegs.  After each guess, you get feedback to guide your next guess, but you only have so many tries to get it right!

Setting up the game:
When you start a new game, you can choose the number of pegs, colors, and guesses, and whether the peg colors are allowed to be duplicated.  These counts are controlled by + and - buttons on the screen, and the duplicate colors option is the button with three pegs.  If it shows duplicate colors, then the solution can have duplicates.  The standard game is 4 pegs, 6 colors, 9 tries, no duplicates, but you can choose from 3 to 6 pegs, 8 to 12 tries, and 6 to 8 colors!

Playing the game:
Once you tap Start, you'll be ready to play!  You start on the bottom row, which will show one peg hole highlighted in yellow.  Tap a color on the right of the screen to set that color peg in the hole and move to the next one.  You can also tap any peg to select it to receive the next color you tap.  You can tap Clear to clear your guess, or tap Guess to submit it.

Scoring your guess:
The smaller pegs to the right of each guess indicate how well you did.  A black peg means one of your pegs is exactly right.  A White peg means one of your pegs is the right color but in the wrong position.  For example, if you have one black and 2 white pegs, that means three of your pegs are the right color, and one of those three is in the right position, with the rest of your pegs the wrong color.

Statistics:
Once you finish a game, you'll have the option of viewing the statistics.  The game keeps track of how many tries it takes to win each game, and how many games you lose, and the statistics screen shows those results.

Play money only. No real-money gambling, no purchases, no prizes. Poker is No-Limit Texas Hold'em on your wrist against one to five computer players, each with a style of its own: the patient Rock, the tight-aggressive regular, the loose-aggressive player, the calling station who never lets go and the maniac who raises everything. They don't see your cards. Before every decision after the flop they deal out the unknown cards hundreds of times against the hands you are likely to hold, weigh the pot odds and decide; on scary boards and in late position they bluff more often, against tight players they give up sooner.

A built-in coach shows your equity and the pot odds while you play, colours the line green when a call is profitable, and after the hand tells you plainly when you folded or called against the numbers. Choose an action by scrolling through Fold, Check or Call and the raise sizes (min, half pot, three quarters, pot, all-in) and confirm, so nothing has to be tapped precisely. Side pots, split pots and the odd chip are handled the way a card room does it.

WHAT IT DOES
- Cash table with 1 to 5 opponents and blinds from 5/10 to 50/100, buy-in 100 big blinds
- Six-player Sit & Go with 1,500 chips, blinds rising every 8 hands up to an ante level, 65/35 payout

- Equity coach with pot odds and a review of your biggest mistake after each hand

- Statistics: VPIP, PFR, bb/100, showdowns won, biggest pot, Sit & Go results and your result per AI style
- Four-colour deck, four table colours, deal speed, all-in confirmation, five languages and a glance with your chip balance

Reactr — how fast are your reflexes?

Green appears. You tap. A number flashes up: your reaction time in milliseconds. Simple to start, surprisingly hard to master — and now it lives on your wrist, no phone needed.

Reactr measures how quickly you respond, then helps you get faster. Tap too early and it catches you out. Tap the moment it turns green and you'll see exactly how sharp you are, with an instant rating from "Sluggish" all the way up to "LIGHTNING".

Five ways to train
- Reaction — the classic: tap the instant the screen turns green.
- Go / No-Go — tap on green, but hold back on red. Trains impulse control, not just speed.
- Choice — one half of the screen lights up; tap the correct side. Trains decision speed.
- Haptic — react to a vibration instead of a color. Eyes-free, and it trains a different sense.
- Test — five rounds in a row for a true average score to beat.

See yourself improve
Every attempt is saved. A clean trend chart shows your moving average over time — a falling line means you're getting faster — with your personal best marked and a consistency score so you can see how steady you are. A daily streak keeps you coming back.

Where do you stand?
Reactr ranks your best reaction against a typical human reaction time and shows your place in the world: Top 10%, Top 5%, Top 1%… climbing the tiers from Rookie to Elite. Chase the next level.

Made for the watch
- Everything runs on the watch — no phone, no account, no sign-up
- A glance shows your best time without opening the app
- Precise millisecond timing, clean dark design

Quick to pick up, easy to obsess over. Reactr turns a spare 30 seconds into a sharper you.

Roem puts Klaverjassen, the Dutch trick-taking card game, on your watch. You play with a computer partner against two computer opponents, by the Amsterdam or the Rotterdam rules, with compulsory or free choice of trump. Roem is counted automatically in every trick: runs of three and four, stuk, four of a kind and four jacks, plus 100 for a pit. The opponents and your partner don't see your cards. During play a coach runs the same calculation in the background, shows the chance that the playing side goes nat, and tells you when another card would have been clearly better. You pick a card by scrolling to it and confirming, so there are no tiny cards to tap, and a game of 16 hands waits where you left it when you close the app.

Reizen is Skat on your watch: a full game against two computer players, played by the International Skat Order. You bid, pick up the skat or play hand, discard two cards, declare a suit game, Grand or Null, and play out the ten tricks. The opponents don't see your cards. Before every move they deal out the cards they can't see in many possible ways, play each version to the end and choose what works best across all of them.

WHAT IT DOES
- Skat for three by the International Skat Order: bidding with all bid values, hand games, Schneider, Schwarz and Ouvert announcements, Grand and Null (hand, ouvert)
- Exact scoring: matadors with or without, multipliers, overbidding, lost games count double

A logic grid puzzle is worth solving only when two things are true of it: exactly one
answer fits the clues, and every clue is needed to get there. A puzzle book runs out
after sixty of them. Generated ones rarely run out, and rarely hold up either: half the
sheet turns out to be clues that were already implied by the clues above them.

Verdix picks the hidden truth first, four suspects paired to four weapons and four
rooms, and then builds the case backwards from it. Candidate clues, all of them true of
that truth, are handed to a solver one at a time until the solver can pin every cell
without guessing. Then the list is walked back through and every clue the solver turns
out not to need is thrown out. What that leaves is a case proved to have exactly one
answer, proved reachable by deduction alone, and stripped of anything decorative: take
away any single clue and it stops being solvable.

WHAT IT DOES
- Every case proved to have one answer and pruned to a minimal set of clues
- Sixteen classes of clue, from a plain denial through either-or, neither-nor, room
  order and adjacency, weapon weight, exactly-one-of and if-then
- Three tick-and-cross grids, paged by a tab strip rather than a swipe, because a swipe
  and a drag are the same gesture until the moment it ends
- Aim, then tap: the first tap frames a cell wider than itself so it stays visible
  around a fingertip, the second cycles it through tick, cross and unknown
- A tick clears the rest of its row and column, which is what a pencil does a second
  later anyway; it can be switched off
- A clue page that shows one clue at a time and files each one away once it is spent
- An accusation names a suspect, a weapon and a room; three wrong calls close the case
  and the grids fill in with the answer
- A hint that names the next cell already forced, and which clue forces it
- A daily case, the same one on every watch, and free cases that never run out
- Best time daily and free, streak, best run, win rate and a difficulty reading
- Five languages, on-watch settings, nothing sent anywhere

WHAT IT NEEDS
Nothing but the watch. No phone, no signal, no account.

besch:
Transform your Garmin watch into a powerful chess training tool. ChessTrainer brings 51 carefully curated and validated chess puzzles directly to your wrist, helping you improve your tactical vision and chess skills wherever you are.

WHAT IS CHESSTRAINER?

ChessTrainer is a dedicated chess tactics trainer designed specifically for Garmin smartwatches. Whether you are waiting for a run to start, taking a break during your workout, or simply have a few spare moments, you can sharpen your chess skills with real tactical puzzles that teach fundamental chess concepts.

COMPREHENSIVE PUZZLE COLLECTION

All 51 puzzles have been programmatically validated for correctness and arranged progressively to build your skills step by step:

Beginner Level (Puzzles 1-20): Start with basic endgame patterns and simple checkmate sequences. Perfect for learning fundamental king and queen coordination.

Intermediate Level (Puzzles 21-40): Progress to tactical captures, opening traps, and forcing checks that create winning advantages.

Advanced Level (Puzzles 41-51): Challenge yourself with complex tactical combinations and sophisticated endgame techniques.

LEARN ESSENTIAL CHESS CONCEPTS

The puzzle collection systematically covers the building blocks of chess mastery:

Checkmate Patterns: Deliver decisive checkmate moves using queen and rook coordination. Recognize unstoppable mating attacks and finish games with confidence.

Endgame Technique: Master the critical skill of converting winning positions. Learn king restriction with checks, optimal queen and rook positioning against lone kings, pawn advancement strategies, and promotion tactics.

Tactical Attacks: Develop your attacking instincts. Exploit the Scholar's Mate pattern and f7/f2 weaknesses, execute powerful queen attacks, identify back rank vulnerabilities, and use forcing checks to gain decisive advantages.

Piece Tactics: Understand how each piece creates threats. Master the devastating knight fork for double attacks, control diagonals with bishops, and learn advanced knight repositioning.

Fundamental Skills: Build a solid chess foundation with proper pawn structure, strategic piece captures and exchanges, and sound opening principles.

PUZZLE CHALLENGES

Train with diverse tactical scenarios including Queen Mate Corner, Scholar's Mate, Knight Fork, Back Rank, Bishop Attack, Rook Final, Italian Attack, King Safety, Pawn Advance, Queen Sacrifice, Open Attack, Knight Tactics, and many more. Each puzzle is named and designed to teach specific patterns you will encounter in real games.

FEATURES

Clear Puzzle Display: Each position shows the chess board with the goal to find the best move. The intuitive interface makes it easy to analyze positions even on a small watch screen.

Button Navigation: Simple controls designed for your Garmin watch. Navigate through puzzles and make your move selections with ease.

Furry Frenzy is a logical, turn-based game where your objective is to guide a mouse to safety, specifically to the exit of the game area. The mouse can only move on the grass. The level is completed if the mouse reaches the exit and has not been eaten by cats. At that point, it will automatically leave the area.

Controls: Use the touch screen to navigate the mouse. The screen is virtually segmented into four areas representing four move directions. See screenshots for details. You can also use the menu to start again from level 1, return to the top reached level, or restart the current one.

Rules: Cats are faster than the mouse; for each turn the mouse takes, cats can move two steps.

Cats always attempt to reach the mouse's coordinates, preferring horizontal moves.

If an obstacle blocks their path, cats cannot navigate around it, which you can use to your advantage.

If a cat reaches a 'cat bed' (red spots), it will sleep there for three turns.

There can be multiple cats, usually two, following the same rules. If two cats occupy the same spot, they merge into a 'super cat'. A super cat does not sleep and moves three steps per turn.

When two cats merge, their turn ends immediately, even if they have not used all their moves.

The first five levels are designed to familiarize you with the game concepts and demonstrate the situations described above.

Enjoy the game.

The capybara crossing game, made for your Garmin watch. Hop your capy across endless roads, rivers and railways. How far can you go?

--- How to play ---

Hop forward to score a point per lane. Cars and trains flatten you. Water swallows you unless you land on a drifting log — and don't drift off the screen. Trees block your path. Stand still too long and the hawk swoops in; a quick hop scares it off. The further you get, the faster the traffic.

--- Unlock 8 capybaras ---

Grab the yuzu fruits scattered across the lanes and spend them on new capybara coats: Classic, Brown, Sand, Grey, Charcoal, Cream, Golden and the exclusive Yuzu capy. 100 yuzus each, all earned by playing — there are no in-app purchases.

--- Your real steps count ---

Once a day, claim a step bonus from the main menu: 1 yuzu for every 100 steps you walked today (up to 50). Walk more, unlock faster.

--- Button controls ---

- START: hop forward
- UP / DOWN: hop left / right
- BACK: hop backward
- MENU (hold UP on most watches): pause

--- Touch controls ---

- Tap the top, left, right or bottom of the screen to hop that way
- Or swipe in any direction

--- Secrets ---

The field hides more than traffic. There is a place you can only reach by going somewhere the game never asks you to go, and it pays you for finding it. The HOW TO screen has a nudge if you get stuck.

--- Saved on the watch ---

Best score, yuzu balance and unlocked capybaras are stored on the watch. Vibration feedback can be toggled from the menu.

--- Requirements and limitations ---

- No internet, account or phone required. The game runs entirely on the watch and never goes online.
- The daily step bonus reads the watch's own step counter; it resets at midnight along with the watch's counters.
- On button-only watches the MENU button (usually a long press of UP) pauses the game; during a run BACK hops backward, so quit through the pause menu.

--- Permissions ---

None. Capy Crossing requests no permissions at all — no location, no heart rate, no network. Steps come from the watch's daily counter, which needs no permission, and nothing ever leaves your watch.

More info: https://silycrafts.com/capy-crossing

A Minesweeper clone for Garmin watches. Adjustable number of mines and board size. The game requires a touch screen. 

The goal of the game is to expose all cells that do not contain a mine. The number on an opened cell without a mine indicates the number of adjancent cells that contain mines. Mines are symbolized with a red "x".

Usage:

Tap on a cell to select it (can be disabled).

Swipe in any direction on the screen to move the cursor and adjust the selection.

Press the physical physical 'Start' button to open the selected cell (right upper button on most watches).

Long press anywhere on the screen to place/remove a flag on the currect cursor position (can be disbaled).  It does not matter where you press as the flag will be always placed/removed at the current cursor position.

Alternatively: Press the physical 'Down' button to place/remove a flag (button not available on all watches).

After a round is finished press the physical button 'Start' to start a new game.

The game will be automatically saved when closing and loaded when reopening the app. You can also start a new game in the settings. 


Settings:

There are three ways to access the settings: 

1) On the watch, press and hold the 'Menu' button (Fenix/Epix/Forerunner etc.: left middle button, Venu/vivoactive: right lower (upper on Venu 2 Sq) button).

2) On the watch, in the game tap the mine icon at the top in the center. The button can be removed in the settings.

3) On your phone, you can change the settings in the ConnectIQ app.

In the settings you can 
    - start a new game
    - adjust the board size (2x2 - 16x16).
    - set the number of mines on the board (0 - 50).
    - enable/disable some of the touch controls.
    - enable/disable the timer
    - disable the settings button
    - see your records in seconds for the given board size and number of mines.

Unfortunately, Venu, Venu 2 and Vivoactive 4 and Vivoactive 5 do not have scalable fonts. For larger board sizes the font size and quality are therefore not optimal on these watches.

Please report any bugs and send me suggestions for improvements.

besch:
The 15 puzzle (also called Gem Puzzle, Boss Puzzle, Game of Fifteen, Mystic Square and many others) is a sliding puzzle which has 15 square tiles numbered 1 to 15 in a frame that is 4 tile positions high and 4 positions wide, with one unoccupied position. Tiles in the same row or column of the open position can be moved by sliding them horizontally or vertically, respectively. The goal of the puzzle is to place the tiles in numerical order (from left to right, top to bottom).

Named after the number of tiles in the frame, the 15 puzzle may also be called a 16 puzzle, alluding to its total tile capacity. Similar names are used for different sized variants of the 15 puzzle, such as the 8 puzzle, which has 8 tiles in a 3×3 frame.

The n puzzle is a classical problem for modelling algorithms involving heuristics. Commonly used heuristics for this problem include counting the number of misplaced tiles and finding the sum of the taxicab distances between each block and its position in the goal configuration.[1] Note that both are admissible. That is, they never overestimate the number of moves left, which ensures optimality for certain search algorithms such as A*.[1]

ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_puzzle

If you enjoy the game, please consider supporting its development with a donation:

How to Play on Touch Devices
Use the screen edges to move the selection cursor.
To select a peg, tap the center of the screen when the cursor is positioned over it.
If the selected peg has only one valid move, the game will perform it automatically.
If multiple moves are possible, the peg will be highlighted in green, and you must choose the destination slot manually by navigating to a valid position.

How to Play on Non-Touch Devices
The upper-left corner of the screen displays the current movement direction.
Press Select to move the cursor in that direction.
Press Next to change the movement direction.
Press Previous to select the currently highlighted peg (if no peg is selected yet).
If the selected peg has only one valid move, the game will perform it automatically.
If multiple moves are possible, automatic movement is disabled. A green selection cursor will appear, allowing you to choose the destination:
Navigate to a valid destination slot.
Press Previous again to confirm the move.
If no valid move is available, the Previous button may also be used to cycle movement directions.

Choose what to produce, then walk. Your steps are converted into materials and XP (10 steps = 1 unit).

naam: d20 Life Counter — Tabletop & Card Game Tracker
besch:
Your life total, on a twenty-sided die, on your wrist.

One number, four buttons, no menus to dig through. The total sits on the top face of a d20, sized to be read at a glance across a table.

HOW IT WORKS

• UP — gain life
• DOWN — lose life
• GPS (top right) — switch between moving by 1 and moving by 5
• Hold UP — start a new game (it asks first, so you can't wipe your total by accident)
• BACK — exit

The step you pick stays put, so a five-point swing is one press and chipping away a point at a time is one press each. The step currently in use is shown at the bottom of the screen.

TRADING CARD GAMES

Starts at 20. Set it to 40 in the Connect IQ phone app for four-player commander-style formats, or anything from 1 to 99 for whatever you're playing. Step by 5 for a big hit, step by 1 for the rest. No more hunting for a spare die, borrowing a pen and paper, or watching someone's phone screen time out mid-turn.

TABLETOP RPGS

Track hit points for your character, or for the monster your table is chewing through. The same two buttons handle a 1-point scratch and a 5-point crit.

BOARD AND CARD GAMES

Anything that counts up and down between 0 and 99 — scores, rounds won, tokens, tickets, tower floors, victory points.

DETAILS

• Your total survives leaving the app. A stray BACK press mid-game doesn't cost you the score — reopen it and you're exactly where you left off. Hold UP when you actually do want to start over.
• Starting life is configurable from 1 to 99 in the Connect IQ phone app, under My Device / My Apps / Life Counter / Settings.
• The number is fitted to the die's top face at runtime, so one-digit and two-digit totals both come out as large as the face allows.
• No ads, no accounts, no network access, and no permissions requested. It doesn't collect anything about you, because there's nothing to collect.
• Supports Instinct 2, Instinct 2S, Instinct 2X, Instinct 3 Solar, Instinct 3 AMOLED, Instinct E, and Descent G1.

undo, restart, jump to any level, language.

Your best move count is kept for every level you finish, and the level list
shows which tens you have cleared. It all stays on the watch - no account, no

2048 is a slide the tiles, equal numbers merge app for Garmin watches.

Slide the four-by-four board in any direction. Tiles run to that side, and two
tiles with the same number become one with twice the number. Every move drops a
new tile. Get to 2048.

Swipe, or tap the edge of the screen on the side you want to slide towards -
tapping is steadier than swiping when you are walking. Press START to take back
the last move; you get one, not a whole history, because undoing further would
let you peek at where the new tile landed and then pick a different direction,
which is a way of winning that stops being a game.

Heads-up Texas Hold'em for Forerunner 55 and Instinct 3 Solar 45/50 mm. Play against the computer offline, or play with one friend in a private online room. Virtual chips only: no real money or purchases. Cards show ranks and drawn suit symbols.

Online: choose Create room on one watch and Join room on the other. Enter the six-digit code with UP/DOWN and START (Forerunner) or GPS (Instinct). The host approves the friend, then both select Ready. Each watch needs a paired internet-connected phone with Garmin Connect able to communicate in the background. No extra phone app or player account is required. This uses the internet, not direct watch-to-watch Bluetooth.

UP/DOWN selects an action; START/GPS confirms. Choose Raise amount to set any legal whole-chip total: UP increases, DOWN decreases, and holding UP cycles adjustment steps of 1, 5, 10, 25 or 50 chips. START/GPS opens an exact-amount confirmation; BACK cancels the editor. Raise To includes your existing contribution this betting round; Add shows the extra chips paid now. Fold and all-in also ask for confirmation. BACK on the table opens details; hold UP outside the editor for the exit menu.

Players start with 200 chips; blinds are 5/10. Both players must select Ready before each online hand. Resume room restores the saved session. Rooms last up to six hours. Each turn allows two minutes: timeout checks if free or folds when facing a bet. Connection interruptions may delay updates. Online availability is subject to service limits; offline computer play remains available. No health or location data is requested.

- Animated ball trails, a changing camera angle and a settling ball.

- A large result number with RED, BLACK or ZERO written underneath.

This is a roulette wheel simulator for entertainment. There is no betting, virtual currency, payout, prize or purchase system.

Open Orbit Roulette from your watch's app list. Press GPS / the upper-right button to spin. Wait for the result, then press it again. Press BACK to leave. Closing during a spin preserves that spin's selected result.

Made exclusively for supported monochrome Instinct watches: Instinct 2, 2S, 2X, Instinct 3 Solar, Instinct E, and monochrome Instinct Crossover. Crossover uses a compact layout below its hand hub. A fishing game for your watch. Cast, wait for the bite, then strike within a second.

The float sits there, twitches once to fool you, then goes under - that is the take. Hook it and the fight starts: every press winds line in, and between presses the fish takes it back. Pull too hard and the line snaps. For fans of arcade fishing games.

- A round runs 30 to 60 seconds, playable while a workout loads
- Bait refills as you go: one every 6 minutes, or every 250 steps
- Catches earn points, points earn tackle: five rods, each bringing new fish
- Eight species from roach to catfish, with a journal of counts and best weights
- A glance shows the creel without opening the game

Controls
START casts, strikes and reels; a tap does the same during a bite or a fight. UP opens the journal, DOWN winds the line in, BACK exits.

Settings
Strike window (Relaxed, Normal, Sharp) and vibration, in Garmin Connect, App Settings.

A daily 5x5 mini crossword for your watch. One grid, ten clues, one a day.

A new crossword every calendar day, 52 in the pack. The clue for the answer you are on
sits above the grid, and that answer is lit up inside it. Fill all nineteen squares correctly
and your streak goes up by one. For Wordle fans who would rather have a grid than a row.

- Crossing letters you already typed are filled in and skipped
- Check letters marks the wrong ones red
- Current streak, best streak, and an optional timer
- Your grid, time and streak are still there tomorrow
- A glance on the watch face says whether today is solved

Controls
UP and DOWN move between the answers. START opens the letter picker: a block of five letters,
then the letter. BACK steps back out, and leaves the game from the grid. Hold the menu button
to check letters or clear an answer.

Settings
Timer and vibration, in Garmin Connect under App Settings. Round watches only.

Classic naval battle vs AI. Hide five ships on a 10 by 10 grid, then trade salvos with the watch until one fleet is gone.

Deploy the fleet by hand or shuffle it, then call each shot row first, cell second. A hit buys another shot. Ships never touch, so the water around a sunk ship opens up at once. For fans of Battleship-style pen-and-paper sea battle games.

- Five ships, 17 cells of 100, the rules everyone already knows
- Three opponents: fires at random, finishes what it hits, or hunts your fleet
- Your steps charge a radar ping that spots one enemy cell and costs no turn
- A battle in progress resumes where you left it, and keeps your record

Controls
START picks the row, then the cell, then fires. UP and DOWN move the cursor and shuffle the fleet. BACK steps back. MENU, a long press on watches with no menu key, opens a new battle and a radar ping.

Settings
Opponent level and vibration, in Garmin Connect, App Settings.

A Uno-style card game for your watch: be first to empty your hand, against one to three bots.

Match the suit or the rank on the pile, or draw. An eight is wild: it plays on anything and renames the suit, and it costs 50 points to be caught holding one.

Your steps are the second resource: every 3000 walked today earn a point of energy, three a day, and a point forces a card that does not match onto the pile.

- A round takes about a minute, a match runs to 100 points
- Four suits of its own - Leaves, Drops, Flames and Stones
- Green frame plays, orange forces for energy, grey is dead
- Deck, discard, hands and score survive leaving the app

Controls
UP and DOWN move along your hand and on to the draw pile. START plays, draws, confirms a suit, starts the next round. Hold UP for the menu, BACK exits.

Settings
Opponents, their skill, vibration and tones, in Garmin Connect, App Settings.

For fans of Uno-style card games and Crazy Eights.

Your daily steps. Your hero’s next adventure.

RPS: Role Playing Stepper turns everyday walking into a fantasy RPG on your Garmin watch. Every step earns 1 EXP, bringing your armored hero closer to the next level. A walk around the block, a busy workday, or a weekend adventure can help you prepare for your next fight.

WALK. LEVEL UP. BUILD YOUR HERO.

Earn an attribute point each time you level up and choose how to grow:
• Strength increases your attack power.
• Defense reduces incoming damage.
• Speed lets you attack more often.
• Health increases how much damage you can withstand.

Each level requires more steps than the last, giving you a long-term adventure to work toward.

BATTLE FANTASY ENEMIES

Watch your hero fight automatically against slimes, goblins, skeletons, and orcs. As you advance, face increasingly difficult encounters with multiple enemies. Time your potions to help survive a close fight.

Win to earn coins and unlock the next encounter. If you fall, keep your equipment, recover, and return ready to try again.

UPGRADE YOUR GEAR

Spend your earned coins on swords, armor, and healing potions. Progress through equipment made from copper, bronze, iron, steel, silver, gold, platinum, and legendary fantasy metals.

Your equipped sword and armor change your hero’s appearance. Keep spare equipment in your pack or sell unused gear for half its purchase price.

TEST YOUR TIMING

Need an extra coin? Play Training Strike, a quick timing challenge. Hit the target zone to earn 1 coin. Miss and lose 1 coin, with your balance never dropping below zero. You can always play, even with an empty purse.

COME BACK TO YOUR ADVENTURE

Your progress saves automatically. Steps recorded by your watch while StepQuest is closed are credited when you return, within the watch’s available activity history.

Between battles, your hero slowly recovers health, and walking helps speed up recovery. Browse your stats, manage your pack, visit the store, or prepare for your next battle from a charming virtual-pet-style home screen.

RPS: Role Playing Stepper makes every walk part of your adventure.

Take the next step. Your hero is waiting.

ORBIWARD transforms your Garmin watch into a complete space defense game.
Your Core is at the center. Enemies attack from every direction. Aim your cannons, let auto-fire do its job, upgrade your arsenal and survive for as long as possible.
MULTIPLE GAME MODES
• CLASSIC: survive increasingly dangerous enemy waves.
• STACK: save upgrades and activate them when you need them most.
• INVASION: reverse the roles and deploy your own enemies against the opposing defense.
• BOSS RUSH: face a series of 14 bosses with unique mechanics.
• DUO VS CPU: fight alongside a second computer-controlled defender.
• ANT DUO: connect two compatible Garmin watches nearby and fight together in the same synchronized game, without a phone or Internet connection.
BUILD YOUR DEFENSE
Kills regularly unlock upgrades including fire rate, damage, additional cannons, projectile penetration, repair, maximum health, shockwave, slowing effects, freeze, automatic turret and an evolving shield.
Build a different defense every run.
VARIED ENEMIES
Enemies don't simply charge toward your Core. Some zigzag or spiral, while others shoot, explode or interfere with your defenses. Their resistance gradually increases and new threats appear the longer you survive.
Three difficulty levels are available: EASY, NORMAL and EXPERT.
ORBITS & SKINS
Earn ORBITS by playing and spend them in the shop to unlock different collections.
Customize your Core, cannons, projectiles, enemies and shield independently.
CUSTOM EDITOR
Create your own skins directly on your watch with the pixel editor. Save multiple creations, then equip, unequip or edit your CUSTOM pieces.
STATISTICS & BESTIARY
Track your performance, records and statistics. End-of-run statistics also show every upgrade in the exact order you obtained it.
Discover enemies and learn their characteristics through the Bestiary.
SAVE & CONTINUE
Stop a game and continue later using multiple save slots. ANT Duo also includes its own continuation system.
CONTROLS
Orbiward is designed for small screens, with touchscreen controls on compatible devices and complete button navigation.
MUSIC & EFFECTS
Compatible Garmin devices feature an original soundtrack inspired by space, arcade games and synthwave.
Sound, music and vibration can be controlled independently.
BUILT FOR GARMIN
Orbiward isn't a phone game squeezed onto a watch. It was designed from the beginning for Garmin: quick sessions, compact interfaces, readable graphics and simple controls.
Full interface available in ENGLISH and FRANÇAIS.
Build your defense. Find your strategy. Survive.
Welcome to ORBIWARD.

What you get:

Every 10 steps is one coin. Not a walker? Floors and active calories count

so a cyclist, a rower or a stair climber earns like a walker. The best of the

watering at any time. Plants need 3 to 10 waterings depending on rarity.

naam: Crafthold 3D – Voxel Island Mine, Build, Craft
besch:

### What you do
- **Dig** anything you can see: turf, wood, stone, coal, iron, gold, gem
- **Build** with what you carry — planks, brick, ladders, doors, obsidian
- **Craft** a workbench, a furnace, a chest, a crop plot and a forge

- **Mine** down through caves to bedrock, 226 metres under the grass
- **Upgrade** your pick and sword through six tiers, wood to Void

- It resolves whether the app is open or not. Come back and read what happened

- Stamina also ticks back on its own while you play

### Controls

  swipe up or down to look

Nine holes of real golf, played over your golfer's shoulder. You stand behind
him at address with the fairway running away to the pin, pick a club, aim it,
swing it — and the camera leaves with the ball, climbing and turning with it
until it lands, bounces and runs out. Par 36, 171 to 548 yards, in clean
flat-shaded 3D on a screen the size of a coin.

A round takes about ten minutes. A hole takes one.

### The swing is three presses
The classic arc meter, on the bezel ring where there is room for it. Press to
start the backswing, press to set the power, press again at the mark. Catch the
mark and the ball goes where you aimed; miss it and your hands put sidespin on
it, and you will watch the ball bend twenty yards into the trees over five
seconds in the air.

Nothing fires itself. The needle runs to the end of the arc, turns round and
comes back for as long as you need, so an interruption costs you time and never
a shot.

### Ten clubs, and the ground is one of them
Driver down to lob wedge, plus a chipper that keeps the ball under the branches
and running, and a putter. The game suggests a club for the yardage and the lie;
taking a different one is usually why you are reading this description.

Every surface plays differently, because the ball keeps moving after it lands.
Fairway gives a long bounce and a proper run-out, rough stops it where it
pitches, sand takes the distance away, the green takes one hop and kills it, and
water costs you a stroke and a drop back down the line. Pines stand in the way,
and a ball that catches one drops out of it. The wind sits on a dial that turns
with your aim, so a crosswind is something you see rather than work out.

A chip can run in from off the green. So can a tee shot, once.

### On the green
A line to set and a pace to find, and pace is the whole putt: dead weight dies
at the cup, anything more runs past, anything less was never going in. The read
shows how far the ball will travel before you hit it — and a better putter buys
more of that read, never a straighter line.

### How to play
- **SELECT**, or a tap in the middle of the screen, does everything: the next
  step, then the three swing presses
- **UP / DOWN**, or the top and bottom of the screen, change club and swing the
  aim — hold them and it keeps turning
- **UP** on a landed tee shot plays a mulligan, if your bag has one in it
- **BACK** for the menu, options and the boards

### Three tees, three different golf courses
Amateur plays the front tees with wide fairways and a breeze. Pro plays the card
as drawn, into fourteen miles an hour. Tour plays the back tees with fairways cut
a fifth narrower and over twenty. Each has its own global board, so an Amateur
round is never compared to a Tour round.

### Modes
- **Round** — nine holes against par
- **Closest to the Pin** — five approaches, scored on the total feet left
- **Daily Round** — the same course, wind and pin for everybody, once a day

### Equipment you earn, not buy
Six pieces, and ever

Fishing from the bow of a bass boat, on your wrist. You look out over the
water the way a bass game always has: weed beds, lily pads, sunken timber and
rock piles between you and the far bank, dark shapes moving under them, and the
yellow ring of your cast waiting on the water. Pick a spot, flick your wrist,
work the lure back, and when the line goes heavy — set the hook and fight it.

A tournament day takes ten minutes. A good fish takes one.

### Cast with your wrist
On watches with a gyroscope you cast like you would with a rod: press SELECT,
then snap your wrist. The harder the flick, the further it goes, and a
half-hearted one lands short. Watches without a gyroscope use the
accelerometer, and every watch can switch to the classic power meter — stop it
on the mark and the lure lands where you aimed.

Cast past the water and you are in the trees. Land it on a fish's head and
it is gone.

### Every lure fishes differently
Eight lures, and each one wants its own retrieve. A worm wants to sit still
between pulls, a spinner and a crankbait want a steady reel, a popper and a
jig want to be twitched. Each one also moves the odds of WHICH fish comes for
it — the pike wants a spoon, the catfish wants live bait, the trophy bass
wants a swimbait. Read the water, pick the cover, pick the lure.

### The fight is the game
A hooked fish runs, rests, charges the boat and jumps. The REEL dial shows the
tension: blue is slack, yellow is working the fish, red is the drag slipping
and the line about to go. Reel while it rests, ease off when it jumps, reel
fast when it comes at you, and steer the rod against every run — tilt the
watch, or use UP and DOWN. Side pressure tires a fish twice as fast. Too
little tension and it spits the hook; too much and the line snaps.

### Six waters, thirty-six species
Mirror Lake, River Bend, the Salt Flats, the Frozen North, the Coral Reef and
the Abyss — from bluegill and largemouth bass to walleye, redfish, lake trout,
grouper, marlin and things that should not live that deep. Six species to a
water, five sizes from runt to legendary. Every new water opens with the total
weight you have landed over your career.

### Your watch changes the bite
Fish 2 reads the real world around you, with nothing extra to install:
- **Time of day** — dawn and dusk are prime time, the midday sun slows the
  bite, and catfish and walleye come out at night
- **Season** — spring fish are heavier, autumn fish feed harder
- **Barometer** — a falling pressure brings the fish on and the big ones up,
  a rising one slows them down
- **Weather** from your phone — overcast and rain are good fishing, and a
  storm front is the best of all
- **Temperature** — warm-water and cold-water species really do prefer it

Watches without a sensor simply fish neutral conditions. The Conditions page in
the Tackle Box tells you what is feeding right now. The Daily Tournament always
fishes neutral conditions, so everybody gets the same day.

### Tackle you earn, never

Forage for food, stockpile wood, and light a campfire. Survive ten nights in the wilderness, right on your wrist.
With only three actions each day, will you search for food or gather wood first? In Camp Days, manage your food, wood, and warmth to face clear skies, wind, and snow—and keep your camp safe through all ten nights.
How to Play
You begin with 5 food, 3 wood, and 6 warmth. Each day, you have three actions. Choose one of the following each time:
- Forage: Gain 3 food, or only 2 when it is snowing.
- Gather Wood: Gain 3 wood to prepare for your next fire.
- Make Fire: Spend 2 wood to restore 5 warmth, up to a maximum of 10. You cannot make a fire without enough wood.
- End Day: Give up your remaining actions and move straight to night.
You can choose the same action more than once. After your third action, night begins automatically.
Watch the Weather and Prepare for Night
Every night consumes 2 food. Warmth loss depends on the weather:
- Clear: Lose 2 warmth.
- Wind: Lose 3 warmth.
- Snow: Lose 4 warmth.
If you do not have enough food to cover the night’s consumption, or your warmth drops to 0 during the night, the challenge ends. Check your supplies and warmth before nightfall, and leave an extra margin for snowy nights.
Controls
Use the up/down buttons or swipe to select an action, then press the confirm button to perform it. On touchscreen devices, you can also tap the left or right side of the bottom action bar to change your selection, then tap the center to confirm.
Press Back or Menu, long-press the screen, or tap the title at the top to open the pause menu. From there, you can resume, view help, or start a new challenge. Your progress is saved automatically so you can continue later.
Plan each day, protect your camp, and see whether you can survive all ten nights.

The man who entered the shop looked as though the road had been trying to kill him for years and had finally grown tired of the effort.

His armor was light, travel-worn, and repaired in more places than it was original. Old scars crossed his hands and jaw, but when he spoke there was no hardness in his voice.

Only weariness.

And beneath it, something gentle.

He set a circular game board on the counter.

“Old?” the shopkeeper asked.

The traveler smiled.

“Older than some men I buried. Younger than others.”

He rested a hand on the board.

“I’ve carried that farther than I care to remember.”

He spoke of long roads, cold camps, wet boots, poor food, and endless watches where nothing happened.

“People remember battles,” he said. “They forget how much of a soldier’s life is spent waiting for one.”

He tapped the board.

“This helped with the waiting.”

He called the game Rotus Maximus.

Simple rules. Quick games. No drawn contests that could stretch on forever.

He had played it with young men on their first campaign, trying not to show how frightened they were. He had played it with old soldiers who could fall asleep sitting upright and somehow wake the instant it was their turn.

He played it with officers over maps while discussing roads, supplies, and battles not yet fought.

Once, he even taught it to an enemy commander.

The shopkeeper raised an eyebrow.

“We were supposed to be discussing where we would meet the following morning.”

“And?”

“We played instead.”

He paused.

“By sunrise, neither of us could think of a good enough reason to start killing each other.”

The shopkeeper looked again at the board.

Cuts scarred its surface. There were burn marks, repairs, and countless scratches around the edge.

Not damage.

History.

“You’re willing to part with it?”

The traveler was quiet for the first time.

“I think I’m finished with roads chosen by other men.”

He wanted a small place somewhere quiet. A roof that did not need to be packed onto a wagon. A table that stayed in one room.

Maybe a garden.

Maybe children, if life was kinder to him than it had been so far.

And he wanted to tell stories.

Not about glory.

About the frightened recruit who became brave. The stubborn general who hated losing. The cook who cheated whenever no one was looking. The enemy who became a friend for the length of a game.

“I’ve spent my life collecting stories,” he said. “I suppose I should put some of them somewhere before I start forgetting the names.”

The shopkeeper disappeared into the back.

When he returned, he carried a bundle wrapped in cloth.

Inside were pale sheets, dark ink, and instruments made for a careful hand.

The traveler touched one of the pages.

Something about it made him hesitate.

The shopkeeper said nothing.

After a moment, the traveler pushed Rotus Maximus across the counter.

“I don’t think I’ll need this where I’m going.”

The shopkeeper looked at the board.

Candy Cascade plays with free in-game credits (CR). There is no real money, no in-app purchases, nothing to cash out and no prizes. Credits have no value outside the game.

FEATURES
- Pay-anywhere wins: 8 or more matching symbols pay, wherever they land.
- Cascades: winning symbols explode and new ones fall in with gravity and bounce, so one spin can win again and again.

- Super Free Spins: 5 or more scatters start free spins where every bomb is x20 or higher.

- Daily bonus: check in every day for 1,000 CR. Day 7 of a streak pays 3,000 CR. Missing a day starts the streak again.

- Bets from 10 to 500 CR.
- Statistics: spins, credits wagered and won, return, biggest win, bonuses, jackpots and best check-in streak, with a reset option.
- Settings: sound (short tones, off by default, on watches with a speaker) and vibration (Strong, Light or Off).

REAL ODDS
Every spin is independent and uses the watch's random number generator. Long-run figures from 10 million simulated spins:
- Free Spins: about 1 in 435 spins (1 in 260 with ante bet).
- Super Free Spins: about 1 in 3,800 spins (1 in 1,900 with ante bet).
- Jackpot wheel: exactly 1 in 5,000 paid spins, at any bet.
- When the wheel appears: MINI 85%, MAJOR 12%, GRAND 2.7%, MEGA 0.3%. The wheel's equal-size sectors are for show; these percentages are the real chances.
- Average return: about 97% of credits wagered (bonus buys about 97%).
The same odds are shown in the game under MENU - Statistics.

HOW TO PLAY
- START or tap the screen: spin. While autospin runs, START stops it.
- UP / DOWN or swipe: change the bet. Tap BET to raise it. Watches without a touch screen play fully with the buttons.
- Tap MENU or hold UP: daily bonus, autospin, bonus buys, ante bet, statistics and settings.
- BACK: leave the game. Your balance and progress are saved on the watch.

Turn your watch into a two-player chess clock. Lay it flat on the table between you and your opponent: the bottom half of the screen is your clock, the top half (turned upside down) belongs to the other player.

Time controls
1+0, 2+1, 3+0, 3+2, 5+0, 5+3, 10+0, 10+5, 15+10 and 30+0 (minutes + seconds per move). "+0" is sudden death.

Increment types

Single or Multiplayer chess on one or two watches in the same room. Can you beat a watch chess app??

You've been wondering what to do on your rest days, now you know! You've been waiting to play chess on your wrist!

Please review so more people can find the app! If you have problems or suggestions please contact the developer directly so I can better assist you. Note the saved game does not affect the watch battery life, it simply uses a very small amount of storage.

Castling! To castle, either move the king two spaces to the side you want to castle, or move the king to the rook square. This alternative is needed in some cases of Chess960 when the pieces are not two spaces apart.

If you have watch to watch connection issues in the same room, try rebooting the watches.

Instructions
1. Start the "Chess" activity from your watch activity page (below activities list) or open the Chess Glance.
2. Select the type of game you want:
* Bot: You vs. the watch! Simple single ply chess engine. (Select difficulty first)
* Two Watches: Normal chess game with two people using two separate watches in the same room.
* Blind Two Watches: Blind chess game with another person on a different watch. Blind chess means you don't get to see your opponent's pieces.
* One Watch: A normal game of chess on a single watch.
3. For Two Watch games, start the same game type on both watches and then wait for the "Waiting for Connection" banner to go away.
4. Movement:
* Cycle through available moves with Up/Down keys (or swiping on some watches). This moves the blue highlight.
* Select a piece to move by pressing the Start key.
* Select the square to move to using the Up/Down keys. This moves the red highlight, and the piece animates to the destination square.
* Move the selected piece by pressing the Start key.
* To go back to piece selection mode, press the Back key.
* Selecting pieces and moving to squares also works by touching the display on watches that have a touch screen.
5. Exit the game by holding down the Up key to return to the Menu (or Menu key on some watches) or by double pressing the Back key.

Gameplay
Only valid moves are selectable. Note that blind chess can be confusing and you will find yourself thinking a move should be valid but the app knows where the pieces are and what the rules are so if you really really think it messed up, convince your opponent to show you their screen.
Pawn promotion always assumes Queen.

About Blind Chess
We used to play blind chess at family gatherings but it was notoriously hard to referee. Playing it on a watch brings back the joy and laughter we shared without the referee saying, "Oh, no! Go back three moves, I messed up!" Blind chess brings together players of all skill levels to use their sleuthing skills in combination with their basic chess knowledge.

The watch lights up a color. Then two. Then three, until you miss one: your

the classic color-sequence mechanic used by dozens of independent games.

# Flappy Bird - Classic Arcade Fun on Your Garmin Watch

Play the addictive Flappy Bird game directly on your Garmin watch! Tap to flap through brick walls, beat your personal best, and compete on global leaderboards.

**The app is FREE to try!** With support for 100+ different Garmin devices, you can test if it works perfectly on your specific watch. Experience classic arcade gaming right on your wrist!

## Features

### Free Features:
- Full gameplay experience
- Tap or button controls to flap
- Progressive difficulty - starts slow, gets faster
- Brick wall obstacles with varying gaps
- Real-time score tracking
- Personal high score system (top 10)

### Pro Features (Unlock After Trial):
- Unlimited play time
- Three difficulty levels (Easy, Medium, Hard)
- Global leaderboards per difficulty
- Compare your scores worldwide
- Compete for top rankings

2. **Tap or press button** to make the bird flap
3. **Avoid hitting walls** - fly through the gaps

5. **Set new records** and climb the leaderboards!

What's in it:
- A daily dive: one new course a day, with a twist of the day, the same for everyone

No account, ads or tracking.

One bird, two pipes and a gap to slip through. Every tap on the screen — or
every button press, if your watch isn't a touchscreen — is one flap. That's it.
You learn it in three seconds and you never master it.

There is more than one flappy in this store. Here is what makes this one
different.

**1. The Daily Challenge is genuinely comparable.**

The challenge pipes are not random. Everyone who plays today meets exactly the
same sequence, on any watch anywhere in the world, and at midnight it changes.
That is why the challenge always runs at **normal difficulty**, whatever you
have set: if one player got the easy gap and another the hard one, the pipes
would land in the same places but it would not be the same game, and the number
would mean nothing.

That is what turns "I got 23" into something you can say out loud. The score
card carries **the date of the challenge**, so a screenshot explains itself:
you can see which day you're talking about.

**2. There is a streak, and the watch reminds you.**

Days in a row playing the challenge. The glance in the carousel tells you when
today's is still pending, without opening anything: turn your wrist, see *PLAY
TODAY*, and you know.

**3. One best score per difficulty, not one for all three.**

From easy to hard the gap narrows by 24% and the speed goes up by 30%: they are
not the same game. With a single number, one afternoon on easy buried whatever
you had done on hard. Here all three sit together in the watch settings.

**4. Medals leave a trace.**

Bronze at 10 pipes, silver at 20, gold at 35, platinum at 60. They don't end
with that run: the watch keeps a count of how many of each you have won, along
with games played, pipes cleared and your streak. A cabinet, not a notification
that disappears.

**5. It is built for your particular watch.**

96 models, from 208 to 486 pixels, round and square, touch and buttons. Nothing
is measured in pixels: everything is a fraction of the screen, and the layout
is checked model by model. Watches without a tone generator don't get shown a
sound setting that would do nothing. Watches that are tight on power drop
background detail by themselves rather than lose the frame rate.

And it is **free** — no ads, no purchases, no account.
---

**Classic.** Random pipes, three difficulty levels, see how far you get. Here
your setting is the one in charge: easy is a way to pass the time, hard asks
for real precision.

The speed creeps up as you clear pipes, so a long run has a shape: the first
twenty are a warm-up and reaching sixty feels earned.

Clipping the edge of the gap sounds and feels different from sailing through
the middle. It seems like a detail and it is half the game.

Everything works with buttons, so it plays the same on watches without a
touchscreen: up and down choose, the action button starts and flaps, back
exits. During a run *any* button flaps, which is what you actually want while
you're falling.

Vibration and sound can be turned off independently,

Turn every spare minute into match day with Flick Scorer, a fast and satisfying football game made for your watch.

Flick from the ball towards goal to take your shot. The direction of your flick controls the placement, while its speed controls the power. Draw a curved path during a free kick to bend the ball around the wall and into the corner. Every shot feels different, and every great finish is yours.

Then step into goal. Watch the striker's run-up, decide where the shot is going and flick your goalkeeper into a full-stretch dive. Think the attacker will aim down the middle? Tap to hold your ground and call their bluff.

Choose your challenge:

- **Penalty** — Five shots against the goalkeeper. Pick your corner, control the power and chase a perfect round.
- **Free Kick** — Lift and curl the ball around a defensive wall before the goalkeeper can reach it.
- **Goalkeeper** — Defend penalties or free kicks by reading the striker and timing your dive.
- **Shootout** — Alternate between shooting and saving. Score more than your opponent over five rounds, then face sudden death if the scores are level.
- **Target Challenge** — Aim for moving targets inside the goal. Hit the centre rings for the biggest points and master smaller targets on harder levels.

Three difficulty levels make Flick Scorer welcoming for quick games and challenging when you want a tougher match. Opponents react faster, clues become less reliable and targets become smaller as the difficulty rises.

Every point rewards skill. Accurate corner shots, controlled power, curved free kicks, quick reactions and difficult saves all score more. String successful attempts together to build a score multiplier. Finish a perfect round, keep a clean sheet or win a shootout for an extra reward.

Your best scores are remembered separately for each way to play and each difficulty, so there is always another record to beat. Quick replay gets you straight into the next round.

Make the game your own with five ball designs and four player styles. Optional wrist vibrations add distinct feedback for goals, saves, shots off the post and perfect rounds.

Play anywhere—no phone, account or internet connection is needed.

Requires a touchscreen watch.

Keywords: football, soccer, penalty, free kick, shootout, goalkeeper, goal, target, arcade, offline, touch, sport, game

Fling Fury is a slingshot game for your watch: pull the bird back, aim, and
let go at fortresses of wood, stone and ice to crush the goblins hiding
inside. Forty levels across four different settings, each one tougher than
the last.

**How to play.** Touch the bird and drag it backwards: the slingshot band
follows your finger, and a dotted arc shows where it's about to fly. Let go
to fire. Wood breaks easily, stone takes several hits, and ice shatters
with anything that breaks at all. Knock out a tower's base and everything
on top comes down - and if it lands on a goblin, that's one down.

**Four worlds, forty levels.** Forest, Desert, Ice and Castle, ten levels
each with their own look. Each world unlocks once every level in the
previous one has earned at least one star. Up to three stars per level,
based on how many birds you have left when you clear it.

**It's the same bird from Flappy Wings**, with an angrier set of eyebrows -
if you've played that one, you'll recognise it instantly.

**Worth knowing before installing.** Touchscreen watches only: the
slingshot is aimed by dragging your finger, and there's no reasonable
button equivalent. The interface text is in English.

WHAT YOU WILL FIND
- Lily pads: safe to bounce on
- Blue pads: they drift from side to side
- Dry leaves: they break when you land on them
- Flowers: good for one single jump
- Mushrooms: a super jump
- Dragonfly: a free ride up, and nothing can hurt you meanwhile
- Bubble shield: saves you from one wasp
- Wasps: pop them with a bubble or land on top of them, but never touch them from below

FEATURES
- Real tilt control using the watch accelerometer
- Automatic calibration: a short countdown takes your current wrist position as "centre", so you can play in any posture
- Prefer buttons? Switch to UP / DOWN control in the settings
- Three tilt sensitivity levels
- The difficulty grows slowly with the height
- A golden line marks your record while you play
- Statistics: best score, games played, wasps popped and total height
- Sounds and vibration can be turned off
- Pause at any time with BACK
- Available in English and Spanish

HOW TO PLAY
- Tilt your wrist: move left and right
- START (or tap): shoot a bubble upwards
- BACK: pause
- Hold UP on the title screen: settings and statistics

One-time purchase: no ads, no subscription, no account and no phone needed. Feedback and ideas are always welcome — leave a review or contact me through the store.

Fruit comes flying up from the bottom of your watch screen.
Swipe across it and it splits in two - flesh, seeds and a
burst of juice. Short rounds made for a spare minute, right
on your wrist.

TWO GAME MODES

- CLASSIC: three lives. Every fruit that falls uncut costs
  one. Bombs appear among the fruit, more often as you go:
  slice one and the game is over. Let it fall and nothing
  happens.
- 60 SECONDS: one minute, no bombs, no lives. Pure scoring.

SCORING WITH TEXTURE

- Slice several fruits in a single swipe to earn combo
  bonuses.
- Keep cutting without missing and your streak raises a
  multiplier, up to x5. Drop a fruit or hit a bomb and it
  resets - every piece matters.
- A rare golden fruit, ringed with sparkles, is worth five
  times a normal one.
- Sometimes three fruits launch together: the perfect combo
  chance, and never with a bomb hidden among them.

MADE FOR YOUR WATCH

- Haptic feedback and custom sound effects: a soft tick per
  cut that rises with your streak, an arpeggio on combos, a
  deep rumble on bombs. Both can be switched off in the
  in-game settings, and both respect your watch system
  settings.
- Best score saved separately for each mode, plus best combo
  and total fruit sliced.

GRID SHEAR is an arcade game for your wrist: steer an energy node out of safe ground, cut a line through open space, and claim whatever you close off while enemies roam the field.

HOW IT PLAYS

The field is a round arena drawn on a fine grid. You start on a strip of captured ground, where nothing can touch you. Press cut and the node leaves safe ground at the next edge, laying a glowing trail behind it. Steer it back onto captured ground and the cut closes: every pocket of open space that holds no enemy becomes yours, so one well-placed line can take several at once. If an enemy touches the node or the trail, or you run into your own trail, a wall or a hazard field, the cut fails and costs one of three energy units.

Reach the target share of the arena to clear the level. Clearing a level gives back one energy unit.

CONTROLS

Three buttons play the whole game. Bottom left turns the node left, bottom right turns it right, and top right cuts. Each press turns exactly a quarter, so two presses reverse. The middle button on the left (UP) pauses, pressed or held, as does a swipe on touch screens. In the menus the same buttons move, select and go back.

On a watch with only two buttons, both on the right, tap the left half of the screen to turn left and the right half to turn right. The lower button also turns right, the upper one cuts, and a swipe pauses.

LEVELS

Three handcrafted levels, each with its own idea. AWAKENING has long straight shelves and open water, and asks for 60%. PRESSURE splits the arena into chambers joined by narrow gates and adds hazard fields, and asks for 70%. OVERDRIVE scatters islands across the field, sends two blades sweeping through the centre, and asks for 80%. Each level adds less starting ground, faster enemies and more of them.

Three kinds of enemy share the field. Drifters bounce in straight diagonals. Hunters steer at your trail while you cut. Interceptors aim at where the node is going, not where it is. Each has its own shape and motion, so none is told apart by colour alone.

SCORING

Every captured cell and every cell of trail scores. Big cuts, very big cuts and close calls with an enemy earn bonuses, clean cuts in a row build a combo up to five times, and later levels multiply everything. A cleared level adds a bonus for the level, for every percent over the target and for every energy unit left. Your high score, best level and best area are kept, and levels unlock as you reach them.

THE LOOK

Black is the canvas. Captured ground is dark teal with a lit cyan edge, open space is near-black with a faint star field, and a pulse of light walks down the boundary. The trail glows cyan while you cut, turns white when it closes, and a wave of light runs through the ground you just took.

SETTINGS

Haptics: on or off.

Sound: on or off.

Contrast: normal or high. High contrast uses flat fills, white edges and no glow, for bright daylight.

Designed for button and touchscreen watches alike - every action works both ways (touch is quickest on touchscreen models).

In menus, left and right move through the items and both together select. On touch screens, hold the left or right half of the screen to steer.

SCORING
