A mint-green laser rotates around the dial. Tap the screen or press START when it reaches the pink target. Every successful hit earns a point, moves the target and reverses the rotation. The laser speeds up and the target gets narrower as your score grows. One mistimed tap ends the run.

Choose your challenge:
- Beginner: a slower laser and a wider target.
- Intermediate: faster timing and a smaller margin for error.
- Extreme: a faster laser and a tighter target from the start.

Enjoy a clean, distraction-free play area, a best score saved on your watch, and a Play again option after each run.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Select a difficulty, then choose Play.
2. Watch the laser approach the pink target.
3. Tap or press START while the laser is inside the target.
4. Keep going as the pace increases. Beat your best and play again.

CONTROLS
- UP / DOWN: navigate the main menu on watches with these buttons.
- START: confirm, start, hit the target or resume.
- BACK: pause during play; return to the menu from the pause or results screen; exit from the main menu.
- Touchscreen: select a difficulty, choose Play and tap during play on supported watches. Touch must be enabled on your device.

DISPLAY AND COMPATIBILITY
Available for the Garmin Connect IQ watch models included in the app's compatible-device list.

The layout adapts to round, rectangular and smaller displays. Monochrome watches use a thicker target segment instead of a pink highlight. Controls and presentation vary by model.

PRIVACY
Laser Spin works offline and does not request network, location or sensor permissions. The app does not send personal data to the developer. Your best score is stored locally on your watch.

KEYWORDS
reflex, timing, arcade, reaction, laser, casual game

LAST COMBAT - a real fighting game, on your watch.

Eight fighters, six stages, a five-cup campaign and a fight loop with actual
depth. No phone, no companion app, no internet - it all runs on the watch.

HOW IT FIGHTS
- Tap the LEFT half to BLOCK
- Tap the RIGHT half HIGH to PUNCH
- Tap the RIGHT half LOW to KICK
- Five buttons work too, if your watch has them

Three inputs, and every one of them is a decision. A punch starts fast and
recovers fast. A kick starts slower but COMMITS sooner, so a kick you have
already thrown survives a trade a punch would lose. Block, and the attacker is
locked out long enough for you to punish - guarding is an opening you create,
not a place to hide.

MASHING STOPS WORKING
This was measured, not guessed - 400 simulated runs per cup. Throwing the same
attack over and over will carry you through the first cup. By the third it
clears about one run in eight, and in the last cup it is as close to zero as
makes no difference. Reading your opponent and mixing your answer is what gets
you through. Turtling never works at all: a round that times out is decided on
remaining health, so you cannot simply wait it out.

THE CAMPAIGN - FIVE CUPS
- ROOKIE (3 fights) - CONTENDER (4) - VETERAN (5) - MASTER (6) - LAST
  COMBAT (7)
- Each cup is a GAUNTLET: its fighters come at you back to back, in order, and
  they get stronger as you go
- One SECOND WIND per cup. Lose a fight and you get one more try at it; lose
  again and the run is over
- Clear a cup to unlock the next, and to be paid for it - 50 coins for ROOKIE
  up to 400 for LAST COMBAT
- Your run is saved after every single fight, so a long-press BACK or a flat
  battery cannot cost you six wins

EIGHT FIGHTERS
JIRO, TENGU, BJORN, NOX, SHROUD, DRAKO, AEGIS and MALVOS. You start with JIRO;
the rest cost 100 coins each. All eight face you as opponents from the very
first fight, so you always know what you are buying.

YOUR STEPS PAY FOR IT
1,000 steps = 5 coins. The count is banked from your daily step total and
backfilled for days you never opened the app, so an ordinary 8,000-step day is
40 coins whether you played or not. A hero is 100. Walk or fight - both work.

ALSO IN THE BOX
- Three difficulties, and they change real numbers: your block holds 1.0 s,
  0.75 s or 0.5 s, and the CPU guards 35 %, 60 % or 85 % of the attacks it sees
- A Training room with a dummy that never hits back
- Best-of-three rounds with a 4-health sudden-death decider
- Six painted stages and a round-screen HUD that actually fits the disc

FREE TRIAL
Want to try the feel first? "Last Combat Trial" is free and gives you the
Training room with the complete fight engine.

Clear the minefield without stepping on a mine. Three board sizes, a daily
challenge and a timer with your best time for each difficulty.

What makes it different:

**You never have to guess.** Before laying the mines, the watch checks that the
board can be solved by reasoning from start to finish. If it can't, it throws it
away and prepares another one. If you lose it's because you got it wrong, not
because the last move was a coin flip.

**The first tap is always safe** and opens an area, so the game starts with
something to work from instead of a lone number in the middle of nowhere.

**Play with your finger or with the buttons.** On watches without a touch
screen the cursor moves with UP and DOWN — hold them to move fast — and START
opens the tile. On touch watches you tap a tile and tap it again to open it;
that confirmation stops a misplaced finger from ending the game on small
screens, and it can be turned off in the settings.

**Tapping an open number clears its neighbours** once all its flags are in
place. It's the move that makes the game fast.

**Your game is not lost** if a notification comes in or you close the app: you
can carry on where you left it. The timer stops meanwhile.

**Daily challenge:** the same minefield for everyone, every day, with a streak
of consecutive days.

The numbers are drawn one by one so they read the same on a 454-pixel watch and
on a 208-pixel one, each in its usual colour.

One watch. Play together.

Turn your Garmin into a pocket-sized game table for friends and family. Multiplayer Games brings seven games to a single watch—no second device, phone connection or account needed.

SEVEN GAMES, ONE WATCH
• Connect Four: take turns dropping discs and connect four across, down or diagonally.
• Tic Tac Toe: a quick head-to-head game of Xs and Os.
• Battleship: confirm your fleet privately, then hunt your opponent's ships on a compact 6×6 board.
• Reaction Duel: wait for GO, then react first. Starting early gives your opponent a point. First to three wins.
• Timing Duel: count in your head and try to stop the hidden timer at a random target between 2 and 7 seconds. Both players get the same target, which changes every round. Compare both players' times and errors.
• Roll or Bank: a dice game for 2–6 players. Keep rolling to grow your turn total, or bank it safely. Roll a 1 and lose the turn's unbanked points. Once a player banks at least 50 points, finish the round so everyone has the same number of turns. The highest final score wins.
• Memory Pairs: reveal cards to find six matching pairs. A match earns a point and another turn. Claim the most pairs to win.

EASY TO SHARE
Memory Pairs and the first five games are for two players; Roll or Bank supports two to six. Play with watch buttons or touch controls on supported devices. Clear turn indicators, results and rematches keep everyone involved.

PLAY OFFLINE
No ads, subscriptions, accounts or online matchmaking. The app does not collect or transmit personal data. Match scores last for the current game session.

Have a game idea, found a bug or want to share feedback? Use Contact Developer in the Connect IQ Store or email ophi.support@gmail.com. Include your watch model when reporting a problem.

Compatibility and language: English is the primary language. The app follows your watch language where translations are available. Designed for the round Garmin watches listed under Compatible Devices. Controls vary by model; touch requires a touchscreen. The interface combines localized turn/result labels with English game titles. Detailed instructions are available in English and German; some text falls back to English in other languages. Battleship requires the other player to look away during private fleet setup. For comparable reaction results, both players should use the same input type.

Turn your Garmin watch into a neon arcade. Neon Apex is an offline car racing game with three scenic courses, three distinctive cars, Quick Race and Time Trial. Dodge traffic, hit rechargeable boost and chase your next personal best—all from your wrist.

THREE ROADS TO MASTER
• Neon City: race through glowing city streets on a 2.3 km course.
• Desert Run: take on sweeping desert curves across 2.8 km.
• Alpine Pass: tackle mountain roads on a 3.1 km course.
Finish Neon City to unlock Desert Run, then finish Desert Run to unlock Alpine Pass.

PICK YOUR CAR
All three cars are available from the start. Choose the balanced Neon Coupe, the agile Cyan Sprint with the strongest handling, or the Red GT with the highest top speed. Each car has its own combination of speed, handling and boost.

TWO WAYS TO RACE
QUICK RACE — Overtake traffic, earn near-miss bonuses and keep collisions down. Finish cleanly to earn three stars.
TIME TRIAL — Enjoy a traffic-free course and race against the clock. Finish with more time remaining to earn more stars.
Choose Easy, Normal or Hard to set the challenge.

BUILT FOR QUICK PLAY
• Automatic acceleration: focus on steering and boost.
• Rechargeable boost: release it to recharge for your next burst.
• Saved progress: keep course unlocks, best stars, scores and times for each course and mode.
• Pause, resume and retry from the in-game pause menu.
• Optional vibration feedback for collisions.
• Offline play, with no phone connection needed during a race.

HOW TO PLAY
Touch: hold the left or right side of the display to steer; hold the center to boost. Release to stop the input. Short taps also provide a brief steering or boost pulse.
Buttons: hold UP to steer left, DOWN to steer right, and START to boost. Press BACK to pause.
Menus: use touch, or UP/DOWN to move and START to select.

HOW TO CUSTOMIZE
Change car: open GARAGE, tap the arrows or use UP/DOWN, then tap SELECT or press START.
Change race mode and difficulty: open PLAY, choose QUICK RACE or TIME TRIAL, choose EASY/NORMAL/HARD, then CHOOSE LEVEL.
Change vibration: open the gear icon on the main menu and toggle VIBRATION. The same menu includes the controls guide and a reset-progress option.

COMPATIBILITY
Designed for supported Garmin AMOLED watches. Check the Compatible Devices list for your exact model. Store previews show the game in the fēnix 9 Pro 51 mm simulator; layouts scale to supported displays.

This is a standalone game app. Watch-face complications and an always-on watch-face mode are not included.

Choose your car. Find your line. Chase your best.

Classic snake, built for a watch instead of ported from a phone.

**It uses the whole screen.** The playfield is a disc that reaches the bezel:
**293 cells**, 49 % more room than the 196 that fit in the largest square you
can inscribe in the same screen at the same cell size. And the wall is the edge
of the watch itself, which is the clearest landmark a round screen has.

**And you can see where you are playing.** The board is drawn —outline, cells
and a light that fades from the centre to the rim—, not hinted at with a grey
that is barely lighter than black. On screens that cannot do that, the field is
marked with the contrast they do have. If your watch falls behind, the game
simplifies the board by itself rather than losing smoothness.

**The controls don't betray you.** Tap the side you want to go to and the snake
goes there: an absolute direction, with nothing to work out about which way it
was facing. Turns are queued, so a turn asked for halfway across a cell isn't lost
and you can chain two of them to take a corner. And a U-turn is never accepted,
because that is the one death that is never the player's fault.

If you prefer something else there are three touch schemes: tap a side, swipe,
or two zones (left and right turn). And on **watches with no touch screen the
game is played with the up and down buttons**, which can be swapped.

**Four bonuses that change the run.** One appears every five apples, each with
its own shape so you can tell them apart at a glance: the **gold** one is worth
five times as much, the **shield** saves you from one crash —and shows as a
ring around the head until you spend it—, the **ghost** lets you pass through
your own tail, and the **triple** multiplies the next three apples by three.
They all expire: you have to go and get them.

**And a combo that rewards taking risks.** Eating another apple before the
combo cools down multiplies your points by up to five. Playing safe in circles
is easy; scoring is not.

**Ten medals** you earn by playing —reach length 100, get saved by a shield,
three daily runs in a row— and **the three best scores of every mode**, not
just the top one.

**Four modes.**

- **Classic**: the wall kills.
- **Tunnel**: leave one side, come back in the other.
- **Walls**: a new block appears every four apples — never in your face, and
  never cutting the field in two.
- **Daily run**: the same game for everyone, changing at midnight, with a
  **streak** of consecutive days that breaks if you skip one.

**Three difficulties, and all of them start slow.** Speed grows with apples,
not with time: if you don't eat, you don't speed up. The arc on the rim shows
how far you are from top speed.

**And the things that matter on a watch**: the snake doesn't move until you
touch something, so opening the app never costs you a game; if you get
interrupted the game is saved and resumed; the best score is kept per mode and
difficulty, because they are not the same game; and golden apples are worth
five ti

One More Run is a reflex game for your watch: you run on your own, forever,
and your only job is to dodge. Switch lanes, jump the hurdles and gaps,
slide under the beams. Each run lasts until the first hit — and it always
feels like one more run.

**How to play.** There's no throttle: speed climbs on its own with distance.
On touchscreen watches, swipe sideways to change lane, up to jump, down to
slide. On button watches, up/down change lane, and the same action button
jumps on a short press or slides while held.

**Four circuits.** The path runs through a sunset canyon, a neon city at
night, snowy peaks and a jungle temple, each with its own palette and
skyline. They rotate every 400 metres, always in the same order, so the
rhythm becomes familiar.

**Coins, gems and two power-ups.** A shield forgives one hit, and a magnet
pulls in coins from any lane for a few seconds and doubles their value. When
an obstacle carries a bonus coin, it sits in the safe lane — the game shows
you the way without needing a HUD for it.

**Streak and multiplier.** Every obstacle you genuinely dodge adds to your
streak, and past twenty in a row it starts multiplying your score, up to
×4. A crash breaks it.

**Free run and daily run.** The daily run hands everyone the same obstacle
sequence each day, so the best distance actually means something. A free
run is saved when you close the app, so you can pick it back up later.

When you stop tapping, the helicopter gradually descends. The current controls use a tap-to-rise mechanic: holding a button or the screen does not make you keep climbing. Maintain your altitude with a steady tapping rhythm.
The passage starts out straight and level, then randomly introduces flat stretches, gentle slopes, and larger rises and dips. As you fly farther, your speed gradually increases and the passage gradually narrows until their limits are reached. After you have flown a certain distance, red enemy aircraft begin approaching from the right. Fly above or below them to get past. Hitting the terrain, the top or bottom edge of the screen, or an enemy aircraft ends the run immediately.
The game offers Easy, Normal, and Hard difficulties. Easy mode has a slower speed, gentler terrain, and enemies that appear later. Hard mode is faster, with more uneven terrain, a passage that narrows more quickly, and enemies that appear earlier. Your score is based on distance flown, with multipliers of 0.7, 1, and 1.3 for Easy, Normal, and Hard respectively. All three difficulties share a single high score stored locally.
From the main menu, you can start a game, change the difficulty, and turn collision vibration on or off. During a game, press Back to pause. After a collision, your score for the run is displayed, with a notification if you set a new record. The game automatically returns to the main menu after about 1.5 seconds. Your high score and settings are saved automatically.
Try to stay near the middle of the passage, watch the terrain ahead on the right, and adjust your altitude with short taps. When an enemy appears, pass it on the side with more space, leaving a safe margin from the upper and lower boundaries.

4. Hold the screen or START to reel. Release to lower the tension. The fish slips deeper while you ease off, so balance progress against the risk of a snapped line.
5. Cast again after each catch. Land three fish before the timer reaches zero.

3. As soon as the screen turns red, press START or tap the screen.

Watch out for false starts: pressing before red ends the round!

Tilt your wrist and a steel ball rolls across the face of your watch. That is
the whole game.

ROLLWERK The Wrist Labyrinth is a labyrinth in the old wooden-box tradition,
rebuilt for a round display and driven entirely by the accelerometer. Dip an
edge and the ball goes that way. It coasts, it drifts wide on a curve, and the
only way to stop it is to tilt back against it. There is no button that moves
the ball.

Twenty hand-built mazes, meant to be played through in order. Each one asks
for something the one before it did not:

• Switchbacks and staircases, where the gaps step across the board and you
  never get a full-width run at anything
• Rings and spokes, where a lap of the watch face replaces a there-and-back
• Spirals of two and three rings, corridors barely wider than the ball
• Timed gates that open and shut on a rhythm you learn by attempt, with a
  warning flash before every one closes, because a door you cannot see coming
  is a trap, not a puzzle
• Holes that pull, and a goal that has to be sunk

The board is a genuine circle, not a rectangle cropped to fit. The rim is part
of the maze.

FEATURES

• Motion control only. No button steers the ball
• 20 levels of escalating difficulty, from a first lesson in coasting to
  three-ring spirals with staggered gates
• Per-level best times, and a clock running while you play
• Picks up where you left off: reopen the app and choose CONTINUE at your
  level or START OVER at level 1
• Three tilt sensitivities (LOW / NORMAL / HIGH), changed mid-run from the
  pause screen
• Calibrates to however your wrist rests: left arm, right arm, sitting,
  standing. Recalibrate at any time
• Keeps the backlight on while the ball is live, so a steady wrist does not
  put the screen to sleep, and stops the moment play stops
• Haptic feedback on a fall and on a finish
• Two hand-built visual designs: a dark machined labyrinth on AMOLED, a
  high-contrast black-on-white instrument dial on MIP, readable in direct
  sunlight
• Goes fully idle on the result screens. No redraws, no sensor, no battery
• Touchscreen devices get tap and swipe for the same actions

CONTROLS

• Tilt the wrist: roll the ball
• START / SELECT: confirm, resume, retry, next level
• BACK: pause; press again to exit
• UP / DOWN: tilt sensitivity, on the pause screen
• Long UP (MENU): recalibrate

NOTES

The accelerometer stays off until you start a run, and is handed back the
moment play stops. Sensor permission is required for the tilt controls and is
used for nothing else. No network access, no data leaves the watch.

The simulator reports a static accelerometer, so the ball will sit still there.
This game only works on a wrist.

Classic arcade air combat
Game Objective
Move your fighter left and right at the bottom of the screen to dodge enemy aircraft and enemy bullets. Your fighter fires automatically, and shooting down a regular enemy earns 1 point. As your score increases, you will advance through waves, enemies will move faster, and bosses will become stronger.
Main Menu
Use the Up or Down button to move the cursor, then press GPS, START, or ENTER to confirm. On touchscreen devices, you can also tap the left or right half of the screen to select the previous or next option.
START: Start the game.
EASY, HARD, EXTREME: Change the difficulty.
VIBRATION ON, VIBRATION OFF: Turn vibration on or off when taking damage and when the game ends.
TILT, BUTTONS/TOUCH: Choose tilt controls or button/touch controls.
HIGH SCORE: View the highest score saved on your device.
In-Game Controls
Your fighter fires automatically, so there is no need to fire manually.
BUTTONS/TOUCH Mode
Hold the Down button to keep moving left.
Hold the Up button or the GPS, START, or ENTER button to keep moving right.
On touchscreen devices, touch and hold the left or right half of the screen to keep moving in that direction. Release to stop moving.
TILT Mode
Tilt the right side of your watch downward by about 5 degrees to move right.
Tilt the left side of your watch downward by about 5 degrees to move left.
Returning your watch to a level position does not stop your fighter immediately. To change its direction of movement, tilt your watch about 5 degrees in the opposite direction.
If the motion sensor is temporarily unavailable, you can use the buttons or tap the left or right half of the screen as an alternative way to control your fighter.
Pausing and Returning
During gameplay, press BACK or ESC twice within 700 milliseconds to pause the game.
On the pause screen, press GPS, START, or ENTER to resume.
On the pause screen, press BACK or ESC to return to the main menu.
When the game ends, GAME OVER appears briefly before the game automatically returns to the main menu.
Health, Score, and Waves
You start each game with 3 health points and can have up to 6 health points.
Colliding with an enemy aircraft or getting hit by an enemy bullet costs 1 health point and resets your weapon to its initial state.
After taking damage, you are invincible for about 5 seconds.
Shooting down a regular enemy earns 1 point. Bosses do not directly add to your score.
Defeating a boss restores 3 health points, up to a maximum of 6.

Sunset Drive is a driving game for your watch with the feel of the late-eighties
arcades: a red convertible, a low sun on the horizon, palm trees on the verge
and a road that keeps twisting while your time runs out.

No story, no long menus. Raise your wrist, start, and twenty seconds later
you're dodging a truck at three hundred kilometres an hour.

**How it plays.** The car accelerates on its own — your job is steering, and
braking when the corner tightens. On touchscreens you steer by holding your
finger on one side; on button watches, with up and down. Running onto the grass
won't stop you, but it drops you to a third of your speed, and those are
seconds you never get back.

**Time is the opponent.** You start with eighteen seconds. Each checkpoint
grants a few more, and every stage grants fewer than the last. Crashing doesn't
end your run — it slows you down, which in the long run is worse.

**The fork.** At the end of every stage the road splits in two and a grass
island forces you to pick a side. There's nothing to press: you choose by
driving. The right branch leads to a tighter course and scores more; the left
one is the quiet route. Every run traces its own path.

**Three ways to play.** Journey chains stages until the clock beats you. Daily
gives everyone the same course each day, so scores are comparable. Time Trial
is a single stage against your own best.

Your run is saved when you quit, so you can stop halfway and pick up where you
left off. There are three difficulty levels, sound and vibration you can set on
the watch itself, and stats for races, distance and streak.

**Worth knowing before you install.** It's a game, so it uses battery while you
play — don't leave it running in the background. On smaller screens the road
draws shorter, though everything stays readable. The interface is in English.

The premier practical tapping game for Garmin watches. TapStage scores speed and accuracy using a hit-factor (tap-factor!) style system inspired by practical shooting sports like IPSC and USPSA. TapStage is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or an official product of IPSC, USPSA, or any affiliated organizations.

PUBLIC BETA  !PLEASE READ!
TapStage is a public beta for testing. It is free during the beta and will become a paid app once testing is complete. Pricing and timing will be announced before that change. Beta scores and leaderboards may be reset during testing. Features, rules and provisional classifier levels may change.

BETA DEVICE COMPATIBILITY
This public beta tests compatibility, touch behaviour and readability across different watch models and screen sizes. Performance and layout may vary. Inclusion in the beta does not guarantee continued support or compatibility with the final paid release. GAMEPLAY
The game consists of stages, or series of targets that appear on order.

Paper targets need two taps; steel targets need one. Centre A taps score 5 points, C taps 3 and D taps 1. Singles score 5 points. A miss costs 5; a No-tap costs 10. When a No-tap appears alone, wait for it to disappear. Net points never fall below zero.

Factor = net points ÷ elapsed seconds.

The falling blocks game, built natively for Garmin watches. Rotate the piece, slide it where it fits, clear the line. Miss a gap and it stays there until you dig it out.

Nothing to set up and nothing to wait for. Press play and you are already in a game.

HOW IT PLAYS

A piece falls from the top, one of seven shapes

Move it left or right, turn it, drop it early if you can see where it goes

Fill a whole row across and the row clears

The stack reaches the top and the game is over

IT GETS FASTER, AND IT DOES NOT STOP

Every ten lines you go up a level, and every level the pieces fall quicker. Level one gives you most of a second to think. By level fifteen you have less than a tenth. There is no level cap and no finish line — the game ends when the stack wins.

Start at level ten if one to nine is not worth your time.

THE BAG IS FAIR

The next piece is not random. All seven shapes are dealt out in a shuffled bag before any of them repeats, so you never sit through five S pieces in a row waiting for the long one. It is the difference between a hard
game and an unfair one.

The NEXT panel shows what is coming, so you can plan two pieces ahead instead of one.

SCORING

One line is 40 points, two is 100, three is 300, four at once is 1200 — all multiplied by your level. Clearing four rows in one drop at level twelve is worth more than forty single lines at level one. That is the whole game in one sentence.

Best score, games played, total lines and best lines in a single game are all kept between sessions.

THE GHOST

An outline shows exactly where the piece will land before you commit. Leave it on while you learn the board and turn it off when you want the points to feel earned.

CONTROLS

Buttons or touchscreen, whichever your watch has, and the game works out which one you have.

On a button watch: down moves left, back moves right, start turns the piece, up drops it faster and holding up drops it all the way. Hold back to pause.

On a touchscreen: tap the left or right of the screen to move, tap the middle to turn, swipe down to drop. Hold your finger on the screen to pause.

MADE FOR THE WATCH

The board is drawn from your screen, not from a fixed grid, so a 218px fēnix and a 454px epix both get the biggest board their screen can hold

Artwork drawn per screen size — nothing is stretched or squashed to fit

On the 64-colour MIP watches the artwork is delivered pre-quantised, so the pieces are clean instead of dithered

Black background: on an AMOLED that is the part of the screen that costs nothing to light

SETTINGS

Starting level, one to ten

Ghost piece on or off

Vibration on or off

Statistics you can reset

NO NONSENSE

No internet. No account. No ads. No lives, no energy, no waiting to play again

The realm of Vael has gone dark, and its great roads — the waymarches — are unlit. Relight them the only way anyone can: by walking. Every real step you take marches your hero down 780 miles of haunted roads. Nothing in Waymarch can be earned at a desk: encounters, levels, and loot unlock at real mile marks, and opening the app more often earns you nothing.

When something blocks the road, the fight resolves the moment you open the app — and it contains a real decision. Strike, Feint, Cast, or Brace: each spends a different resource with its own economy (stamina from steady walking, tricks from places you stop, spell slots that recharge on rest days and trickle back per 4,000 steps). Read the enemy right and you win clean. Read it wrong and you bleed, lose supplies, and it keeps the road. Or swallow your pride and slip past — for a price.

Three classes with subclass forks, permanent either/or talents (one can be re-forged at each waystone — life changes over a months-long game), a perk tree with real tradeoffs, gear sets, and twelve biomes that each punish somebody’s build. No single answer works everywhere: the deepwood swallows spells, the barrows blunt steel, the frost stiffens clever fingers.

Finish the campaign and it echoes: a harder, remixed run that carries one heirloom and a permanent sigil forward. Built for months of real walking — a 3,000-step day and a 15,000-step day both always have something to chase.

Built for the wrist: no phone app, no account, no network, no background battery drain. Your save lives on the watch, survives reboots and updates, and steps can never be double-counted — the ledger reconciles against Garmin’s own daily step counts, once. Works on MIP and AMOLED, buttons or touch.

Easy to start. Hard to put down.

Wristling is a tiny pixel pet that lives on your watch and grows with your everyday activity.

Your steps feed it. It dozes off at the bedtime set in your user profile. When your stress level runs high it gets frazzled, and it perks up when your energy is good.

Hatch it with 5,000 steps. About a week after the egg appears, your sprout grows up into the kind of mover you are: a Goat if you climb lots of floors, a Sprinter if you rack up intensity minutes, a Wanderer if you just keep walking. What will yours become?

Tap the screen (or press UP or DOWN) and it jumps for joy, unless it is fast asleep. It blinks, looks around and hops about on its own, under a sky that follows the time of day.

Take it for a walk from the menu (press START). The walk is recorded as a normal walking activity, and every whole kilometre of a saved walk earns it a treat.

Having a slow day while your energy is low or your stress is high? It rests with you instead of getting upset. Stay under a quarter of your step goal for five days running, though, and it goes foraging until you reach half your goal again. It never dies.

Good to know
• Wristling is a game for fun. It is not a medical or health product and does not diagnose, monitor or treat anything.
• It reads the steps, step goal, floors, intensity minutes, stress and energy levels your watch already records, plus the bedtime in your user profile. It does not track sleep.
• Walks use GPS and heart rate, and are saved as normal activities that sync to Garmin Connect like any other.
• Stress and energy need a watch that records them.
• Your pet catches up whenever you open the app. Open it on days you feel run down so it knows to rest with you.
• Privacy: Wristling itself sends nothing anywhere. No account, no ads, no analytics, no phone connection needed.
• Free, with no in-app purchases.

Wristling was inspired by my two daughters, and it is dedicated to them.

Cheat sheet and game companion for the Czech word game Země-Město (Country-City, a Scattergories-style game). Pick a letter and the watch shows Czech words for 12 categories: country, city, river, colour, name, animal, currency, food, brand, singer, thing and musical instrument.
THREE MODES
Cheat sheet: a category list with the first answer, or a full-screen card with several words.
Coach: the watch draws a letter and a category and asks you. START reveals the answers, UP means "I got it" and the score counts.

Over 1,500 Czech words for 30 letters including Č, Ř, Š and Ž. Works offline, no phone needed, nothing leaves the watch.

WATCHES
130 Garmin watches: fēnix 5 to 9, epix, Forerunner, Venu and Venu Sq, vívoactive, MARQ, Enduro, Descent, Approach, D2, Instinct 2, 3 and E and more.

Royal Draw is multi-hand video poker for your wrist. You get one hand, choose which cards to HOLD and press DRAW. Your held cards are copied into 3, 5 or 10 hands, and every hand draws its replacements from its own deck. Then watch each hand slide in, flip and show what it won.

GAMES
- Jacks or Better 9/6 (99.54% return with optimal play)
- Bonus Poker 8/5 (99.17%)
- Deuces Wild NSU, deuces are wild (99.73%)
Return figures are the published values for these pay tables with optimal strategy and a 5 CR bet per hand. Results of every hand are random (system cryptographic random source).

HOW IT PLAYS
- Choose 1, 3, 5 or 10 hands and 1-5 CR per hand (up to 50 CR per deal).
- Royal Flush pays 4000 CR only at 5 CR per hand, like a real machine.
- 3 and 5 hands are shown as rows above your hand; 10 hands play out on a sliding stage and fill a 3 x 3 results grid.
- Big wins get a full-screen celebration with vibration.

EXTRAS
- Coach tips: marks the recommended hold (simplified expert strategy; optional).
- Double Up after a win: pick a card higher than the dealer's (optional).
- +250 CR daily bonus, a daily task and 12 achievements with CR rewards.
- Card backs and table colours you unlock with CR.
- Statistics: deals, hands, your return, biggest win and hand counts per game.
- Glance shows your balance and whether today's bonus is waiting.
- Settings: sound, vibration, animation speed (normal, fast, off), Coach, Double Up.

CONTROLS
Touch: tap cards to hold, tap DRAW, tap the balance for the pay table, swipe left to change hands.
Buttons: UP/DOWN move, START holds or draws, hold UP for the menu. Fully playable on watches without a touchscreen.

CREDITS ARE VIRTUAL
CR are play credits only. They cannot be bought, have no cash value and cannot be exchanged for money or prizes. There are no in-app purchases and no network access. This is a game for entertainment, not gambling.

d100 as a pair of percentile dice: 00 and 0 read as 100

Defend the orbit. Intercept the drones.

At the centre of the ring, the reactor wakes. Drones emerge from its core and head for the boundary. Your ship circles the reactor: find the right angle and intercept them before they escape.

In Nova Strike Game, your weapons fire automatically. Position is everything: one well-timed turn, one target lined up, a few more points. You start with three lives. Every drone that crosses the boundary costs one, and the pressure builds the longer you last.

Bonuses can change your next few moments: an extra life, faster projectiles or a higher fire rate. Use that opening to stay in the game and push past your personal best.

One life left. A drone nears the edge. Time for one more turn? Enjoy a short arcade session on your Garmin watch, then come back for another attempt. Your best score stays saved locally.

Five-button watches: UP/DOWN to turn, START to play or pause. Two-button models: main button to turn left, back button to turn right, hold MENU to pause. The MENU button depends on the model; see COMMANDES.md. While paused: main button to resume, back to exit.

Buttons only. No touch controls. Offline play, no account or online leaderboard. Only the best score is saved after closing. Uses the watch language: French, English, German, Italian, Portuguese or Spanish; English fallback.

Twelve quiet islands lie beyond the shore, waiting for your first camp. A walk around the neighbourhood, a longer route home, a few extra steps during the day: little by little, your everyday journeys provide the resources for a new adventure. Where will you build a farm, and which island will get the next lighthouse?

Use new steps recorded by your Garmin watch to develop your archipelago. Manage wood and stone, choose your buildings and gradually open the way to all twelve islands. Control the adventure entirely with the watch’s physical buttons. Your progress is saved, ready for your next visit.

A source is waiting, but the route ahead is broken. Pipes point in every direction, and the destination sits just beyond a maze of possibilities. Turn one piece and watch the connected path grow. Change another and an unexpected route appears. The moment everything joins up is yours to discover.

Work through 40 puzzles on compact 4 × 4 grids. Use the physical UP and DOWN buttons to select a tile, then press START to rotate its pipe. Undo a move, restart a puzzle, or chase a better move record. Your current game is saved, ready for the next quiet moment with your watch.

The next roll could fill your purse—or cost you a life. Three dice, three lives and six stages stand between you and the end of the expedition. The gold keeps growing, the target draws closer, and another roll starts to look irresistible. Will you know when to stop?

Roll the dice, reach the stage target, then decide whether to keep going or bank your haul. A single 1 wipes out your unbanked gain and costs one life; banked gold stays safe. Make every decision with your Garmin watch’s physical buttons. Your expedition and dice roll are saved so you can continue where you left off.

Two blue heroes, a handful of red enemies, and nineteen hexes: this battlefield fits on your wrist, but every decision matters. Move into position, strike a neighboring opponent, or hold your ground and guard. Both heroes get one action before the enemy takes its turn, making coordination the heart of each skirmish.

Twelve missions challenge you to read the terrain and make the most of your small squad. Available spaces guide your choices, with every action controlled by physical buttons and no touchscreen input. Victories unlock the next mission and record your best turn count. Saved progress also lets you return in the middle of a team turn.

A door opens, an enemy waits, and your supplies will only last so long. Eight rooms stand between you and the dungeon’s guardian. Every opponent reveals the next counterattack, leaving you to judge when to strike, raise your guard, or spend a precious healing potion. One careful choice can keep the expedition alive.

Between rooms, camp gives you another decision: recover your strength, sharpen your blade, or improve your armor. Turn-based combat lets you consider every move at your own pace. Play entirely with physical buttons, with no touchscreen controls. Your progress is saved so you can return to the adventure and try to beat your best score.

Two crates need moving, and their destinations look close enough. Then a narrow passage changes the plan. Push too soon and the route behind you may disappear. Walk around, find the right approach, and picture where each crate must go next. This little warehouse rewards the player who thinks one move further ahead.

Explore 20 original levels on compact 6 × 6 boards. Choose a direction with the physical UP and DOWN buttons, then press START to move or push. Crates can be pushed but never pulled. Undo a mistake, restart a tricky layout, and improve your move records. Your game is saved between sessions.

Six letters form a small circle on your wrist. One word catches your eye, another begins to take shape, and suddenly an ordinary pause becomes a little search for hidden possibilities. Look again: the letters have not changed, but there may be more waiting among them than you first imagined.

Build words of at least three letters and find five to move to the next puzzle, or keep searching for more. Explore 20 puzzles in each of five languages: French, English, German, Spanish and Italian, with 100 puzzles altogether. Use your watch’s physical buttons to choose letters and submit words. Your discoveries and progress are saved separately for each language.

At first, all you have is an empty grid and a handful of numbers. One row begins to make sense. A column confirms your idea, and a hidden pattern slowly takes shape. There is a quiet satisfaction in watching an image emerge from nothing but careful deduction, one square at a time.

Discover 36 puzzles on 5 × 5 grids, each with a unique solution. Move the cursor with the physical UP and DOWN buttons, then use START to fill a square, mark it empty, or clear it. Compare row and column clues, undo changes when needed, and return to your saved progress whenever you have a spare moment.

Round Billiards is a carom game on a round table that fits your round watch screen. Hit both red balls with the white ball in one shot to score a point and shoot again. Miss and you lose one of your 10 turns. How many points can you make in 10 turns?

**Features**
- **Round table:** a lit blue felt, black chrome rail with yellow diamond sights and glossy 3D balls. The round cushion sends balls back toward the centre, so bank shots feel different from a straight rail.
- **Aim:** a dotted guide runs to where the white ball first hits, and an arrow shows where the struck red ball will go. On touch watches tap or drag where you want to shoot; UP/DOWN fine-tune by 1 degree.
- **Power:** press START and the power band at the bottom fills and drains. Press START again at the right moment.
- **Spin:** set follow, draw or side spin on the small white ball at the lower left (Settings on watches without touch).
- **Two rules:** Both reds (basic) and Cushion first (touch a cushion before the first red). Pick one on the start screen with UP/DOWN; best scores are kept per rule.
- **Score at a glance:** a band of turns left along the top with a big score, and at the end your score on a big billiard ball with a "New best!" badge.
- Game history, help pages with figures, English and Korean.

**How to use**
1. On the start screen pick a rule with UP/DOWN and press START.
2. Aim by tapping or with UP/DOWN, then press START for the power band.
3. Press START at the power you want. When the balls stop, the shot is judged. Hold UP for the menu, BACK to exit.

**Good to know**
- No sensors, no location, nothing is saved to Garmin Connect.
- Free with no ads. Use Donate in the menu if you would like to support the app.

CHOOSE. ADAPT. REACH THE FINISH.

No run required: play it on the couch, on the train or the night before your own race.

MAKE EVERY CHOICE COUNT

Push the pace or save your legs? Grab a gel or keep moving? Follow the group or trust your own plan? Manage Time, Sugar, Water, Legs and Morale through handcrafted situations, real course landmarks and the surprises of race day. Your preparation shapes the start. Your decisions shape the finish.

BEAT YOUR BEST. GIVE YOUR FRIENDS A SCORE TO CHASE.

Every race has its own online leaderboard. Compare results with your running friends, climb the rankings and come back with a better race plan. Your score rewards both your finish time and the reserves you bring across the line. The right choice at the right moment can make all the difference.

Pick your next start line and see how far your judgement takes you.

Pour coloured water between tubes until every tube holds one colour. A calm, satisfying puzzle, made for your wrist.

No pain, no chips.

Sweat Casino is a mini casino on your wrist that you can only play by working out. Every intensity minute your watch records becomes a chip: 1 minute = 1 chip. Once your balance hits zero, the only way back to the tables is to go and sweat.

GAMES

Blackjack: double down, split, and blackjack pays 3:2. Cards are dealt with animations and the dealer's hidden card flips over.
European roulette: animated 37-pocket wheel. Bet on a single number, red/black, odd/even, low/high (1-18 / 19-36) or dozens.
Coin flip: double or nothing.

HOW CHIPS WORK

100 welcome chips on first launch.
Each time you open the app, new intensity minutes from the current week turn into chips, with a "+N chips" animation.
A minute is never paid twice. The weekly counter resets on Monday, like on your watch.
Minutes stop paying once your balance reaches 500 chips, so you can't stockpile by just opening the app. Winnings at the tables have no cap.
Hit zero and you get the "NO PAIN, NO CHIPS" screen. Go train, then come back.
CONTROLS Works with buttons on every watch (START to confirm, UP/DOWN to choose, BACK to go back) and with taps and swipes on touchscreen models.

GOOD TO KNOW

No real money, no purchases, no ads, no betting of any kind: chips have no value outside the app.
No permissions requested and no data leaves your watch. Your balance is stored locally.
